    "S4": [("H9", 1), ("H6", 9), ("H7", 10), ("H2", 10), ("H8", 7), ("H5", 10),
           ("H10", 8), ("H4", 3), ("H3", 7), ("H1", 10)],
    "S5": [("H9", 6), ("H10", 10), ("H2", 7), ("H8", 7), ("H5", 5), ("H7", 4),
           ("H3", 7), ("H4", 7), ("H1", 10), ("H6", 7)],
    "S6": [("H9", 6), ("H4", 6), ("H8", 8), ("H1", 10), ("H7", 5), ("H5", 10),
           ("H10", 9), ("H3", 2), ("H6", 1), ("H2", 2)],
    "S7": [("H5", 5), ("H3", 7), ("H10", 5), ("H6", 2), ("H2", 9), ("H1", 10),
           ("H8", 1), ("H9", 1), ("H4", 3), ("H7", 4)],
    "S8": [("H2", 8), ("H7", 10), ("H3", 2), ("H6", 9), ("H5", 4), ("H9", 9),
           ("H8", 8), ("H1", 3), ("H4", 8), ("H10", 10)],
    "S9": [("H6", 8), ("H4", 10), ("H3", 3), ("H1", 7), ("H8", 1), ("H9", 9),
           ("H7", 1), ("H2", 9), ("H5", 4), ("H10", 9)],
    "S10": [("H10", 6), ("H6", 4), ("H1", 2), ("H7", 7), ("H2", 4), ("H8", 3),
            ("H5", 4), ("H4", 8), ("H3", 10), ("H9", 7)]
}

# Compute a safe big‑M (sum of all processing times)
big_M = sum(p for ops in shipments.values() for (_, p) in ops)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Shipment_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = {}
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for idx, (h, p) in enumerate(ops):
        var_name = f"start_{s}_{idx}"
        start[(s, idx)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for each pair of shipments that share a hub
order = {}  # key = (s_i, s_j, hub) with s_i < s_j alphabetically
for hub in {h for ops in shipments.values() for (h, _) in ops}:
    # collect all (shipment, op_index) that use this hub
    ops_on_hub = [(s, idx) for s, ops in shipments.items()
                  for idx, (h, _) in enumerate(ops) if h == hub]
    # create binary var for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_hub)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_hub)):
            s_i, idx_i = ops_on_hub[i]
            s_j, idx_j = ops_on_hub[j]
            # enforce a deterministic ordering of the key to avoid duplicates
            key = (s_i, s_j, hub) if s_i < s_j else (s_j, s_i, hub)
            var_name = f"y_{key[0]}_{key[1]}_{hub}"
            order[key] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job (shipment) precedence constraints
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for idx in range(len(ops) - 1):
        p = ops[idx][1]
        model += (start[(s, idx)] + p <= start[(s, idx + 1)],
                  f"prec_{s}_{idx}")

# 2) Disjunctive (no‑overlap) constraints on each hub
for hub in {h for ops in shipments.values() for (h, _) in ops}:
    # list of operations on this hub
    ops_on_hub = [(s, idx, p) for s, ops in shipments.items()
                  for idx, (h, p) in enumerate(ops) if h == hub]
    for i in range(len(ops_on_hub)):
        s_i, idx_i, p_i = ops_on_hub[i]
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_hub)):
            s_j, idx_j, p_j = ops_on_hub[j]
            key = (s_i, s_j, hub) if s_i < s_j else (s_j, s_i, hub)
            y_ij = order[key]

            # i before j  (y_ij = 1)  or j before i (y_ij = 0)
            model += (start[(s_i, idx_i)] + p_i <= start[(s_j, idx_j)] + big_M * (1 - y_ij),
                      f"no_overlap_{s_i}_{idx_i}_before_{s_j}_{idx_j}")
            model += (start[(s_j, idx_j)] + p_j <= start[(s_i, idx_i)] + big_M * y_ij,
                      f"no_overlap_{s_j}_{idx_j}_before_{s_i}_{idx_i}")

# 3) Definition of makespan
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    last_idx = len(ops) - 1
    last_p = ops[last_idx][1]
    model += (Cmax >= start[(s, last_idx)] + last_p,
              f"Cmax_def_{s}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

# Print start times in a readable order
for s in sorted(shipments.keys()):
    print(f"Shipment {s}:")
    for idx, (hub, p) in enumerate(shipments[s]):
        st = pulp.value(start[(s, idx)])
        print(f"  Op {idx+1} ({hub}, {p})  start = {st:.2f}, finish = {st + p:.2f}")
    print()

    model += start[b] + p_b <= start[a] + big_M * y_var, f"Machine_{b}_before_{a}"

    last_op = op_id[(j, 4)]
    _, _, _, p_last = rev_op[last_op]
    model += Cmax >= start[last_op] + p_last, f"Makespan_job{j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (total completion time): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times for each shipment operation:")
for i in range(1, num_ops + 1):
    j, k, m, p = rev_op[i]
    print(f"  Shipment S{j} - operation {k} (Checkpoint {m}, time {p}) : start = {pulp.value(start[i]):.2f}")

print("\nOrdering decisions (y = 1 means first operation before second):")
for (a, b), y_var in y.items():

        j2, k2, m2, _ = rev_op[b]

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 4 shipments (jobs) and 4 customs checkpoints (machines).
Objective: minimise the makespan (completion time of the last shipment).

The model uses start‑time variables for each operation, binary ordering variables for
pairs of jobs that share a machine, and a makespan variable Cmax.
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# jobs : list of (machine, processing_time) in the required order
jobs = {
    "S1": [("C2", 1), ("C3", 7), ("C1", 7), ("C4", 6)],
    "S2": [("C1", 9), ("C4", 10), ("C3", 2), ("C2", 4)],
    "S3": [("C1", 5), ("C3", 3), ("C4", 2), ("C2", 8)],
    "S4": [("C4", 5), ("C3", 8), ("C1", 2), ("C2", 5)],
}

machines = ["C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"]
jobs_list = list(jobs.keys())
num_ops = 4                     # each job has exactly four operations

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper dictionaries
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# processing time p[(j,op_index)]
proc = {}
# machine used m[(j,op_index)]
mach = {}
# for each machine, list of (job, op_index) that use it
ops_on_machine = {m: [] for m in machines}

for j in jobs_list:
    for idx, (m, t) in enumerate(jobs[j]):
        proc[(j, idx)] = t
        mach[(j, idx)] = m
        ops_on_machine[m].append((j, idx))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Customs_Shipment_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# start time variables (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    [(j, idx) for j in jobs_list for idx in range(num_ops)],
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# binary ordering variables for each unordered pair of jobs sharing a machine
Y = {}
for m in machines:
    ops = ops_on_machine[m]
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for k in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            j1, idx1 = ops[i]
            j2, idx2 = ops[k]
            # enforce a consistent ordering (j1 precedes j2 or vice‑versa)
            var_name = f"Y_{j1}_{j2}_{m}"
            Y[(j1, j2, m)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence within each job (operations must follow the given order)
for j in jobs_list:
    for p in range(num_ops - 1):
        model += (
            start[(j, p)] + proc[(j, p)] <= start[(j, p + 1)],
            f"Job_{j}_prec_{p}",
        )

# 2) Disjunctive (machine) constraints using big‑M formulation
M = 200  # big enough (greater than total processing time of all jobs)

for m in machines:
    ops = ops_on_machine[m]
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for k in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            j1, idx1 = ops[i]
            j2, idx2 = ops[k]

            # Ensure consistent ordering variable exists (j1<j2 alphabetical)
            if (j1, j2, m) in Y:
                y = Y[(j1, j2, m)]
            else:
                # the reverse key – we created only one direction
                y = Y[(j2, j1, m)]

            # j1 before j2 on machine m
            model += (
                start[(j2, idx2)]
                >= start[(j1, idx1)] + proc[(j1, idx1)] - M * (1 - y),
                f"Machine_{m}_{j1}_before_{j2}",
            )
            # j2 before j1 on machine m
            model += (
                start[(j1, idx1)]
                >= start[(j2, idx2)] + proc[(j2, idx2)] - M * y,
                f"Machine_{m}_{j2}_before_{j1}",
            )

# 3) Makespan must be at least the completion time of each job's last operation
for j in jobs_list:
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[(j, num_ops - 1)] + proc[(j, num_ops - 1)],
        f"Makespan_bound_{j}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in time units):")
for j in jobs_list:
    for p in range(num_ops):
        s = pulp.value(start[(j, p)])
        m = mach[(j, p)]
        t = proc[(j, p)]
        print(f"  {j} - operation {p+1} on {m} (proc {t}): start = {s:.2f}")

# optional: show ordering decisions
print("\nMachine order decisions (Y variables):")
for key, var in Y.items():
    j1, j2, m = key
    print(f"  {j1} before {j2} on {m}: {int(pulp.value(var))}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop model for the four cargo shipments (S1‑S4) that must pass
through four customs checkpoints (C1‑C4) in a given order.
The model minimises the makespan (total completion time).

PuLP with the HiGHS solver is used.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# processing times (in the order the operations are listed below)
proc = [
    1, 7, 7, 6,      # S1
    9,10, 2, 4,      # S2
    5, 3, 2, 8,      # S3
    5, 8, 2, 5       # S4
]

# machine (checkpoint) for each operation
machine = [
    "C2","C3","C1","C4",   # S1
    "C1","C4","C3","C2",   # S2
    "C1","C3","C4","C2",   # S3
    "C4","C3","C1","C2"    # S4
]

num_ops = len(proc)                     # 16 operations
ops = range(num_ops)

# precedence inside each shipment (job)
job_ops = {
    "S1": [0, 1, 2, 3],
    "S2": [4, 5, 6, 7],
    "S3": [8, 9,10,11],
    "S4": [12,13,14,15]
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Cargo_Shipments_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", ops, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Big‑M (larger than any possible schedule length)
M = sum(proc) + 1   # 85

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job‑precedence constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for job, seq in job_ops.items():
    for a, b in zip(seq[:-1], seq[1:]):          # a must finish before b starts
        model += start[b] >= start[a] + proc[a], f"Prec_{job}_{a}_before_{b}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Machine capacity (no overlap) – binary ordering variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each checkpoint collect the operations that need it
machine_to_ops = {}
for i, m in enumerate(machine):
    machine_to_ops.setdefault(m, []).append(i)

# binary variable y_{i,j}=1 if i precedes j on the same machine
y = {}
for m, ops_on_m in machine_to_ops.items():
    # create a binary variable for every unordered pair on this machine
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_j = ops_on_m[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op_i}_{op_j}"
            y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

            # i before j
            model += (
                start[op_i] + proc[op_i] <= start[op_j] + M * (1 - y[(op_i, op_j)]),
                f"Mach_{m}_{op_i}_before_{op_j}"
            )
            # j before i
            model += (
                start[op_j] + proc[op_j] <= start[op_i] + M * y[(op_i, op_j)],
                f"Mach_{m}_{op_j}_before_{op_i}"
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Definition of makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for job, seq in job_ops.items():
    last_op = seq[-1]
    model += Cmax >= start[last_op] + proc[last_op], f"Makespan_{job}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (total completion time): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times of each operation (operation index : (Shipment, Checkpoint, Processing, Start)):")
op_to_job = {}
for job, seq in job_ops.items():

for i in ops:
    job, pos = op_to_job[i]
    print(f"Op {i:2d} : ({job}, {machine[i]}, p={proc[i]}, start={pulp.value(start[i]):.2f})")

        machine[(j, idx)]   = m

# -----------------------------

s = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("s", ops, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 4 shipments (jobs) through 4 customs checkpoints (machines).
Each operation must be processed without interruption, each checkpoint can handle only
one operation at a time. The model minimizes the makespan (total completion time).

The model uses:
  - Continuous start‑time variables   s[(i,k)]  ≥ 0
  - Binary ordering variables         y[(i,k,j,l)] ∈ {0,1}
  - Continuous makespan variable      Cmax

PuLP with the HiGHS solver solves the MILP.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs (shipments) indexed 0..3, operations indexed 0..3 (their order)
# Each operation: (machine, processing_time)
jobs = {
    0: [("C2", 1), ("C3", 7), ("C1", 7), ("C4", 6)],   # S1
    1: [("C1", 9), ("C4",10), ("C3", 2), ("C2", 4)],   # S2
    2: [("C1", 5), ("C3", 3), ("C4", 2), ("C2", 8)],   # S3
    3: [("C4", 5), ("C3", 8), ("C1", 2), ("C2", 5)],   # S4
}

machines = ["C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"]

# Pre‑compute processing times p[(i,k)] and machine assignment m[(i,k)]
p = {}   # processing time
m = {}   # machine
for i, ops in jobs.items():
    for k, (mach, time) in enumerate(ops):
        p[(i, k)] = time
        m[(i, k)] = mach

# Big‑M value – larger than any possible schedule length
M = sum(p.values()) + 10   # 84 + 10 = 94, safe bound

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Customs_Checkpoint_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# Start time of each operation (continuous, ≥0)
s = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          ((i, k) for i in jobs for k in range(4)),
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary ordering variables for every pair of operations that share a machine
y = {}
for mach in machines:
    # collect all operations that require this machine
    ops_on_mach = [(i, k) for (i, k), mm in m.items() if mm == mach]
    # create binary variable for each unordered pair
    for idx1 in range(len(ops_on_mach)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops_on_mach)):
            i1, k1 = ops_on_mach[idx1]
            i2, k2 = ops_on_mach[idx2]
            var_name = f"y_{i1}_{k1}_before_{i2}_{k2}"
            y[(i1, k1, i2, k2)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job precedence constraints (operations must follow given order)
for i, ops in jobs.items():
    for k in range(len(ops) - 1):
        model += (
            s[(i, k + 1)] >= s[(i, k)] + p[(i, k)],
            f"Precedence_job_{i}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# 2) Machine capacity (no overlap) using ordering binaries
for mach in machines:
    ops_on_mach = [(i, k) for (i, k), mm in m.items() if mm == mach]
    for idx1 in range(len(ops_on_mach)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops_on_mach)):
            i1, k1 = ops_on_mach[idx1]
            i2, k2 = ops_on_mach[idx2]
            y_var = y[(i1, k1, i2, k2)]

            # either (i1,k1) finishes before (i2,k2) starts, or vice‑versa
            model += (

        f"Makespan_bound_job_{i}",

model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal" or status == "Feasible":
    print(f"Minimum makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax):.2f}\n")
    for i in sorted(jobs):
        print(f"Shipment S{i+1}:")
        for k, (mach, _) in enumerate(jobs[i]):

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 4 shipments (jobs) and 4 customs checkpoints (machines).
Each shipment must follow a given sequence of (machine, processing time) pairs.
Goal: minimise the makespan (completion time of the last shipment).

Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs are indexed 0..3, machines 1..4 (C1..C4)
jobs = {
    0: [(2, 1), (3, 7), (1, 7), (4, 6)],   # S1
    1: [(1, 9), (4,10), (3, 2), (2, 4)],   # S2
    2: [(1, 5), (3, 3), (4, 2), (2, 8)],   # S3
    3: [(4, 5), (3, 8), (1, 2), (2, 5)],   # S4
}

num_jobs = len(jobs)
num_ops_per_job = 4

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper structures
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# (job, op_index) -> (machine, proc_time)
op_info = {}
# machine -> list of (job, op_index) that use it
machine_ops = {1: [], 2: [], 3: [], 4: []}

for j, ops in jobs.items():
    for k, (m, p) in enumerate(ops):
        op_info[(j, k)] = {'machine': m, 'proc': p}
        machine_ops[m].append((j, k))

# Big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(p for ops in jobs.values() for (_, p) in ops) + 10  # 84+10 = 94

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Customs_Shipment_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = {}
for j in range(num_jobs):
    for k in range(num_ops_per_job):
        var_name = f"start_{j}_{k}"
        start[(j, k)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
y = {}
for m, ops in machine_ops.items():
    # create unordered pairs (i1,i2) with i1 < i2 for uniqueness
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops)):
            (j1, k1) = ops[idx1]
            (j2, k2) = ops[idx2]
            var_name = f"y_{j1}_{k1}_{j2}_{k2}_m{m}"
            y[(j1, k1, j2, k2, m)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job‑order (precedence) constraints
for j in range(num_jobs):
    for k in range(num_ops_per_job - 1):
        p = op_info[(j, k)]['proc']
        model += (
            start[(j, k)] + p <= start[(j, k + 1)],
            f"Job_{j}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# 2) Machine capacity (disjunctive) constraints using binary ordering variables
for m, ops in machine_ops.items():
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops)):
            (j1, k1) = ops[idx1]
            (j2, k2) = ops[idx2]
            p1 = op_info[(j1, k1)]['proc']
            p2 = op_info[(j2, k2)]['proc']
            yvar = y[(j1, k1, j2, k2, m)]

            # if y = 1 then operation (j1,k1) precedes (j2,k2)
            model += (
                start[(j1, k1)] + p1 <= start[(j2, k2)] + M * (1 - yvar),
                f"Machine_{m}_order_{j1}_{k1}_before_{j2}_{k2}",
            )
            # if y = 0 then operation (j2,k2) precedes (j1,k1)
            model += (
                start[(j2, k2)] + p2 <= start[(j1, k1)] + M * yvar,
                f"Machine_{m}_order_{j2}_{k2}_before_{j1}_{k1}",
            )

# 3) Makespan definition
for j in range(num_jobs):
    last_k = num_ops_per_job - 1
    p_last = op_info[(j, last_k)]['proc']
    model += (
        start[(j, last_k)] + p_last <= Cmax,
        f"Makespan_job_{j}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal" or status == "Feasible":
    print(f"Minimum makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax):.2f}\n")
    print("Start times of each operation (job, operation index):")
    for j in range(num_jobs):
        for k in range(num_ops_per_job):
            s = pulp.value(start[(j, k)])
            m = op_info[(j, k)]['machine']
            p = op_info[(j, k)]['proc']
            print(
                f"  Job {j+1} Op {k+1} (Machine C{m}, proc={p}) -> start = {s:.2f}"
            )
else:
    print("No feasible solution found.")

# Job‑shop scheduling model for four shipments and four customs checkpoints.
# Solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver.

import pulp
import itertools

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs (shipments) are indexed 0..3.
# Each job is a list of (checkpoint, processing time) in the required order.
job_ops = {
    0: [("C2", 1), ("C3", 7), ("C1", 7), ("C4", 6)],   # S1
    1: [("C1", 9), ("C4", 10), ("C3", 2), ("C2", 4)],  # S2
    2: [("C1", 5), ("C3", 3), ("C4", 2), ("C2", 8)],   # S3
    3: [("C4", 5), ("C3", 8), ("C1", 2), ("C2", 5)],   # S4
}

machines = ["C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"]
jobs = list(job_ops.keys())

# Helper dictionaries
proc_time = {}          # processing time p[i,k]
machine_of = {}         # machine m[i,k]
op_index = {}           # for each (job, machine) gives the operation index k

for i in jobs:
    for k, (m, t) in enumerate(job_ops[i]):
        proc_time[(i, k)] = t
        machine_of[(i, k)] = m
        op_index[(i, m)] = k

# Big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(t for _, t in itertools.chain.from_iterable(job_ops.values())) + 1   # 84+1 = 85

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("cargo_schedule", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    [(i, k) for i in jobs for k in range(4)],
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary variables to decide the order of two jobs on the same machine
Y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Y",
    [(i, j, m) for i, j in itertools.combinations(jobs, 2) for m in machines],
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise the makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job‑internal precedence constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for i in jobs:
    for k in range(3):               # three precedence links per job
        model += (
            S[(i, k + 1)] >= S[(i, k)] + proc_time[(i, k)],
            f"Job_{i}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Machine capacity constraints (disjunctive constraints)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for i, j in itertools.combinations(jobs, 2):
    for m in machines:
        # operation index of job i on machine m
        ki = op_index[(i, m)]
        kj = op_index[(j, m)]
        pi = proc_time[(i, ki)]
        pj = proc_time[(j, kj)]
        Si = S[(i, ki)]
        Sj = S[(j, kj)]

        # If Y[i,j,m] = 1 then i precedes j on machine m
        model += (
            Si >= Sj + pj - M * (1 - Y[(i, j, m)]),
            f"Machine_{m}_i{ i }_after_j{ j }_ifY0",
        )
        # If Y[i,j,m] = 0 then j precedes i on machine m
        model += (
            Sj >= Si + pi - M * Y[(i, j, m)],
            f"Machine_{m}_j{ j }_after_i{ i }_ifY1",
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for i in jobs:
    last_op = 3
    model += (
        Cmax >= S[(i, last_op)] + proc_time[(i, last_op)],
        f"Makespan_job_{i}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve with HiGHS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output the schedule
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in time units):")
for i in jobs:
    print(f"Shipment S{i+1}:")
    for k in range(4):
        m = machine_of[(i, k)]
        st = pulp.value(S[(i, k)])
        pt = proc_time[(i, k)]
        print(f"  Operation {k+1} on {m}: start = {st:.2f}, duration = {pt}")
    print()

# Uses PuLP with the HiGHS solver

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs (shipments) are indexed 0..3, machines (checkpoints) 1..4
jobs_data = {
    0: [  # S1
        (2, 1),   # (Checkpoint C2, processing time 1)
        (3, 7),
        (1, 7),
        (4, 6),
    ],
    1: [  # S2
        (1, 9),
        (4, 10),
        (3, 2),
        (2, 4),
    ],
    2: [  # S3
        (1, 5),
        (3, 3),
        (4, 2),
        (2, 8),
    ],
    3: [  # S4
        (4, 5),
        (3, 8),
        (1, 2),
        (2, 5),
    ],
}

# Big‑M value – larger than any possible makespan
M = 100

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build sets of operations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# each operation is identified by a tuple (job, op_index)
operations = []                     # list of all (job,op) tuples
proc_time = {}                      # processing time for each operation
machine_of = {}                     # machine used by each operation

for j, seq in jobs_data.items():
    for k, (m, p) in enumerate(seq):
        op = (j, k)
        operations.append(op)
        proc_time[op] = p
        machine_of[op] = m

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Customs_Checkpoint_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          operations,
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# makespan (continuous, >=0)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
Y = {}
for m in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    # operations that need machine m
    ops_on_m = [op for op in operations if machine_of[op] == m]
    # create a binary variable for each ordered pair (i before j)
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_j = ops_on_m[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
            Y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each job (must follow the given order)
for j, seq in jobs_data.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        op_curr = (j, k)
        op_next = (j, k + 1)
        model += (
            S[op_curr] + proc_time[op_curr] <= S[op_next],
            f"Job_{j}_seq_{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# 2) Machine capacity constraints (no overlap on the same checkpoint)
for (op_i, op_j), y_ij in Y.items():
    # op_i before op_j when y_ij = 1
    model += (
        S[op_i] + proc_time[op_i] <= S[op_j] + M * (1 - y_ij),
        f"Mach_{machine_of[op_i]}_{op_i}_before_{op_j}",
    )
    # op_j before op_i when y_ij = 0  (equivalently y_ij = 1 forces the opposite)
    model += (
        S[op_j] + proc_time[op_j] <= S[op_i] + M * y_ij,
        f"Mach_{machine_of[op_j]}_{op_j}_before_{op_i}",
    )

# 3) Makespan must be at least the completion time of each job
for j, seq in jobs_data.items():
    last_op = (j, len(seq) - 1)
    model += (
        Cmax >= S[last_op] + proc_time[last_op],
        f"Makespan_job_{j}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (job, operation index) -> start")
for op in sorted(operations):
    print(f"  Job {op[0]+1}, Op {op[1]+1}: start = {pulp.value(S[op]):.2f}")

# Optional: detailed schedule per checkpoint
print("\nSchedule per checkpoint:")
for m in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    ops_on_m = [op for op in operations if machine_of[op] == m]

        start = pulp.value(S[op])
        finish = start + proc_time[op]
        print(f"    Job {op[0]+1} (Op {op[1]+1}) [{start:.2f}, {finish:.2f}]")

    "S4": [("C4", 5), ("C3", 8), ("C1", 2), ("C2", 5)],
}

# op_id = (job, index) where index starts at 0
operations = {}
for job, ops in jobs.items():
    for idx, (machine, proc) in enumerate(ops):
        operations[(job, idx)] = {"machine": machine, "proc": proc}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    for idx in range(len(ops) - 1):

            start[nxt] >= start[cur] + operations[cur]["proc"],
            f"Precedence_{job}_{idx}_to_{idx+1}",

    # If y = 1, op_a finishes before op_b starts
    model += (
        start[op_a] + proc_a <= start[op_b] + M * (1 - y_var),
        f"Machine_{operations[op_a]['machine']}_order1_{op_a}_{op_b}",

    # If y = 0, op_b finishes before op_a starts
    model += (
        start[op_b] + proc_b <= start[op_a] + M * y_var,
        f"Machine_{operations[op_a]['machine']}_order2_{op_a}_{op_b}",
    )

# 3. Makespan definition: Cmax must be at least the completion time of each job
for job, ops in jobs.items():
    last_op = (job, len(ops) - 1)
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[last_op] + operations[last_op]["proc"],
        f"Makespan_bound_{job}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in the same time units as processing times):")
for (job, idx) in sorted(start.keys()):
    st = pulp.value(start[(job, idx)])
    proc = operations[(job, idx)]["proc"]
    mach = operations[(job, idx)]["machine"]
    print(f"  {job} operation {idx+1} on {mach}: start = {st:.2f}, duration = {proc}")

for job, ops in jobs.items():
    last = (job, len(ops) - 1)
    comp = pulp.value(start[last]) + operations[last]["proc"]
    print(f"  {job}: completion = {comp:.2f}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for the four shipments (S1‑S4) and four
customs checkpoints (C1‑C4).  The model minimizes the makespan (total
completion time) using PuLP and the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs = ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"]
machines = ["C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"]

# (machine, processing time) in the required order for each shipment
operations = {
    "S1": [("C2", 1), ("C3", 7), ("C1", 7), ("C4", 6)],
    "S2": [("C1", 9), ("C4", 10), ("C3", 2), ("C2", 4)],
    "S3": [("C1", 5), ("C3", 3), ("C4", 2), ("C2", 8)],
    "S4": [("C4", 5), ("C3", 8), ("C1", 2), ("C2", 5)],
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper structures
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# start[(job,op_index)] – continuous start time of that operation
start = {}
# map (job, machine) -> (op_index, processing_time) for quick lookup
job_machine_to_op = {}

for job, ops in operations.items():
    for idx, (mach, proc) in enumerate(ops):
        start[(job, idx)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"start_{job}_{idx}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
        job_machine_to_op[(job, mach)] = (idx, proc)

# List of all binary ordering variables y[(i,j,m)] where i<j
order = {}
# big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = 200  # safe upper bound (total processing time = 84)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("customs_jobshop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variable: makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("makespan", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
model += Cmax, "Minimize makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job precedence constraints (operations must follow the given order)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for job, ops in operations.items():
    for k in range(len(ops) - 1):
        _, proc_k = ops[k]
        model += (
            start[(job, k + 1)] >= start[(job, k)] + proc_k,
            f"precedence_{job}_op{k}_to_op{k+1}",
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Machine capacity constraints (no overlap on the same checkpoint)
#    For each unordered pair of jobs that share a machine we introduce a
#    binary variable y indicating which job is processed first.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for mach in machines:
    # collect jobs that need this machine
    jobs_using = [j for j in jobs if (j, mach) in job_machine_to_op]
    # create ordering variables for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(jobs_using)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(jobs_using)):
            job_i = jobs_using[i]
            job_j = jobs_using[j]
            var_name = f"y_{job_i}_{job_j}_{mach}"
            y = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")
            order[(job_i, job_j, mach)] = y

            # retrieve operation indices and processing times
            op_i_idx, p_i = job_machine_to_op[(job_i, mach)]
            op_j_idx, p_j = job_machine_to_op[(job_j, mach)]

            # i before j  ->  start_i >= start_j + p_j  (if y = 0)
            model += (
                start[(job_i, op_i_idx)] >= start[(job_j, op_j_idx)] + p_j - M * (1 - y),
                f"machine_{mach}_{job_i}_after_{job_j}",
            )
            # j before i  ->  start_j >= start_i + p_i  (if y = 1)
            model += (
                start[(job_j, op_j_idx)] >= start[(job_i, op_i_idx)] + p_i - M * y,
                f"machine_{mach}_{job_j}_after_{job_i}",
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Makespan definition – Cmax must be at least each job's completion time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for job, ops in operations.items():
    last_idx = len(ops) - 1
    _, last_proc = ops[last_idx]
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[(job, last_idx)] + last_proc,
        f"makespan_ge_{job}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in time units):")
for job in jobs:
    ops = operations[job]
    for idx, (mach, proc) in enumerate(ops):
        st = pulp.value(start[(job, idx)])
        print(f"  {job} - operation {idx+1} on {mach} (proc={proc}): start = {st:.2f}")

print("\nMachine order decisions (y = 1 means first job precedes second job):")
for (i, j, mach), var in order.items():
    print(f"  {mach}: {i} before {j} ? {int(pulp.value(var))}")

    7: [("DC2", 9), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 5), ("DC8", 8),
        ("DC5", 2), ("DC9", 2), ("DC1", 3), ("DC6", 9)],
    8: [("DC1", 5), ("DC5", 8), ("DC3", 1), ("DC7", 9), ("DC6", 9),
        ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 6), ("DC8", 5), ("DC4",10)],
    9: [("DC6",10), ("DC2", 5), ("DC7", 5), ("DC3", 8), ("DC1", 1),
        ("DC4", 8), ("DC9", 3), ("DC5", 4), ("DC8", 6)]
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Sets, parameters and big‑M
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
operations = []                 # list of (truck, index) tuples
proc_time   = {}                # processing time of each operation
machine     = {}                # centre (machine) of each operation
total_time  = 0                 # sum of all processing times (used for big‑M)

for t, seq in truck_routes.items():
    for k, (cent, p) in enumerate(seq, start=1):
        op = (t, k)
        operations.append(op)
        proc_time[op] = p
        machine[op]   = cent
        total_time   += p

# big‑M large enough to dominate any feasible schedule
BIG_M = total_time

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# 3.1 Decision variables
# start time of each operation
start = {(t, k): pulp.LpVariable(f"s_{t}_{k}", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')
         for (t, k) in operations}

# makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a centre
order = {}   # key = (i, j) with i < j (lexicographically)
centres = {c for c in machine.values()}          # set of all centres
for cent in centres:
    ops_at_c = [op for op in operations if machine[op] == cent]
    for i in range(len(ops_at_c)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_at_c)):
            op_i = ops_at_c[i]
            op_j = ops_at_c[j]
            var = pulp.LpVariable(
                f"y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}",
                cat='Binary')
            order[(op_i, op_j)] = var

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.1 Precedence constraints inside each truck
for t, seq in truck_routes.items():
    for k in range(1, len(seq)):
        op_curr = (t, k)
        op_next = (t, k + 1)
        model += (start[op_next] >= start[op_curr] + proc_time[op_curr],
                  f"Precedence_T{t}_op{k}_to_{k+1}")

# 5.2 Machine capacity (disjunctive) constraints
for (i, j), y_ij in order.items():
    # i before j  (y_ij = 1)  -> start_j >= start_i + p_i
    model += (start[j] >= start[i] + proc_time[i] - BIG_M * (1 - y_ij),
              f"Cap_{machine[i]}_{i}_before_{j}")
    # j before i  (y_ij = 0)  -> start_i >= start_j + p_j
    model += (start[i] >= start[j] + proc_time[j] - BIG_M * y_ij,
              f"Cap_{machine[i]}_{j}_before_{i}")

# 5.3 Definition of makespan
for op in operations:
    model += (Cmax >= start[op] + proc_time[op],
              f"Makespan_def_T{op[0]}_op{op[1]}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Optimal makespan =", pulp.value(Cmax))

# (optional) print start times in a readable order
print("\nStart times (truck, operation index) -> start")
for t in sorted(truck_routes):
    for k in range(1, len(truck_routes[t]) + 1):
        op = (t, k)
        print(f"  T{t} op{k}: {pulp.value(start[op]):.2f}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Scheduling model for 9 trucks each visiting 9 distribution centers.
Goal: minimise the makespan (completion time of the last handling operation).
The model uses start‑time variables (continuous) and binary ordering variables
for every pair of operations that share the same centre.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are indexed 1..9, each has 9 stops (order matters).
# For each truck we list the centre (as a string) and the handling time.
truck_routes = {
    1: [("DC1", 4), ("DC3", 4), ("DC7", 8), ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 5),
        ("DC6",10), ("DC4", 6), ("DC5", 9), ("DC8", 6)],
    2: [("DC8", 1), ("DC1",10), ("DC2", 9), ("DC7", 2), ("DC6",10),
        ("DC5",10), ("DC9", 7), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8)],
    3: [("DC7",10), ("DC1", 5), ("DC6", 9), ("DC5", 5), ("DC9", 7),
        ("DC3",10), ("DC4", 9), ("DC8", 1), ("DC2", 8)],
    4: [("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 8), ("DC3", 2), ("DC5",10), ("DC8", 5),
        ("DC1", 6), ("DC2", 2), ("DC6", 7), ("DC9", 6)],
    5: [("DC1", 1), ("DC2", 1), ("DC7", 5), ("DC6", 8), ("DC3", 2),
        ("DC9", 9), ("DC5", 1), ("DC4", 8), ("DC8", 4)],
    6: [("DC5", 5), ("DC9", 6), ("DC7", 1), ("DC3",10), ("DC2",10),
        ("DC4",10), ("DC6", 5), ("DC8", 2), ("DC1", 6)],
    7: [("DC2", 9), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 5), ("DC8", 8),
        ("DC5", 2), ("DC9", 2), ("DC1", 3), ("DC6", 9)],
    8: [("DC1", 5), ("DC5", 8), ("DC3", 1), ("DC7", 9), ("DC6", 9),
        ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 6), ("DC8", 5), ("DC4",10)],
    9: [("DC6",10), ("DC2", 5), ("DC7", 5), ("DC3", 8), ("DC1", 1),
        ("DC4", 8), ("DC9", 3), ("DC5", 4), ("DC8", 6)]
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper structures
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a flat list of operations indexed by (truck, position)
ops = {}                     # (t,k) -> {'center':..., 'dur':...}
center_to_ops = {}           # centre -> list of (t,k)

for t in range(1, 10):
    for k, (c, d) in enumerate(truck_routes[t], start=1):
        ops[(t, k)] = {'center': c, 'dur': d}
        center_to_ops.setdefault(c, []).append((t, k))

# Upper bound on the schedule horizon (big‑M)
# Sum of all processing times = 516 (computed from the data above)
BIG_M = 516

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Start time of every handling operation
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", ops.keys(), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of every operation must be before the makespan
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
for (t, k), data in ops.items():
    model += S[(t, k)] + data['dur'] <= Cmax, f"makespan_bound_t{t}_k{k}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Precedence constraints inside each truck (order must be respected)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in range(1, 10):
    for k in range(1, 9):               # 1..8, because we look at k and k+1
        dur = ops[(t, k)]['dur']
        model += S[(t, k + 1)] >= S[(t, k)] + dur, f"precedence_t{t}_k{k}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Disjunctive (resource) constraints for each centre
#    For every unordered pair of operations that use the same centre we
#    introduce a binary variable y_ij that decides the processing order.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
Y = {}   # (i,j) -> binary variable, where i < j in a deterministic ordering

def op_index(op):
    """Return a unique integer for sorting (truck,position) pairs."""
    t, k = op
    return (t - 1) * 9 + (k - 1)   # 0‑based index from 0..80

for centre, op_list in center_to_ops.items():
    # there are exactly 9 operations per centre
    for i in range(len(op_list)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(op_list)):
            op_i = op_list[i]
            op_j = op_list[j]

            # create binary variable y_ij  (1 → i before j)
            var_name = f"y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
            Y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

            dur_i = ops[op_i]['dur']
            dur_j = ops[op_j]['dur']

            # i before j  OR  j before i
            # i before j  :  S_i + p_i <= S_j   (enforced when y_ij = 1)
            model += (S[op_i] + dur_i <= S[op_j] + BIG_M * (1 - Y[(op_i, op_j)]),
                      f"order1_{var_name}")

            # j before i  :  S_j + p_j <= S_i   (enforced when y_ij = 0)
            model += (S[op_j] + dur_j <= S[op_i] + BIG_M * Y[(op_i, op_j)],
                      f"order2_{var_name}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum makespan =", pulp.value(Cmax))

# Optional: print start times in a readable order
print("\nStart times (Truck, Step):")
for t in range(1, 10):
    for k in range(1, 10):
        print(f"Truck {t:>1} Step {k:>1} -> Start = {pulp.value(S[(t, k)]):6.2f}  "
              f"(Centre {ops[(t, k)]['center']}, Dur {ops[(t, k)]['dur']})")

# 3. Model

Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# 3.3 Binary ordering variables for every pair of operations that share a centre
y = {}

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop model for the 9‑truck, 9‑center problem.
All data are entered directly in the script.
The model is solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. DATA
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# routes : list of trucks, each truck is an ordered list of (center, processing time)
routes = {
    1: [("DC1", 4), ("DC3", 4), ("DC7", 8), ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 5),
        ("DC6",10), ("DC4", 6), ("DC5", 9), ("DC8", 6)],
    2: [("DC8", 1), ("DC1",10), ("DC2", 9), ("DC7", 2), ("DC6",10),
        ("DC5",10), ("DC9", 7), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8)],
    3: [("DC7",10), ("DC1", 5), ("DC6", 9), ("DC5", 5), ("DC9", 7),
        ("DC3",10), ("DC4", 9), ("DC8", 1), ("DC2", 8)],
    4: [("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 8), ("DC3", 2), ("DC5",10), ("DC8", 5),
        ("DC1", 6), ("DC2", 2), ("DC6", 7), ("DC9", 6)],
    5: [("DC1", 1), ("DC2", 1), ("DC7", 5), ("DC6", 8), ("DC3", 2),
        ("DC9", 9), ("DC5", 1), ("DC4", 8), ("DC8", 4)],
    6: [("DC5", 5), ("DC9", 6), ("DC7", 1), ("DC3",10), ("DC2",10),
        ("DC4",10), ("DC6", 5), ("DC8", 2), ("DC1", 6)],
    7: [("DC2", 9), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 5), ("DC8", 8),
        ("DC5", 2), ("DC9", 2), ("DC1", 3), ("DC6", 9)],
    8: [("DC1", 5), ("DC5", 8), ("DC3", 1), ("DC7", 9), ("DC6", 9),
        ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 6), ("DC8", 5), ("DC4",10)],
    9: [("DC6",10), ("DC2", 5), ("DC7", 5), ("DC3", 8), ("DC1", 1),
        ("DC4", 8), ("DC9", 3), ("DC5", 4), ("DC8", 6)]
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. BUILD OPERATION LIST
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ops = []                     # each element will be a dict describing an operation
op_id = 0
for truck, seq in routes.items():
    for pos, (center, proc) in enumerate(seq):
        ops.append({
            "id"      : op_id,
            "truck"   : truck,
            "pos"     : pos,          # position inside the truck route (0‑based)
            "center"  : center,
            "proc"    : proc
        })
        op_id += 1

N = len(ops)                 # total number of operations (=81)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. PRECEDENCE RELATIONS (within each truck)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
precedences = []             # list of tuples (i , j) meaning i must finish before j starts
for truck, seq in routes.items():
    # collect operation ids for this truck in order
    ids = [op["id"] for op in ops if op["truck"] == truck]
    ids.sort(key=lambda i: ops[i]["pos"])
    for a, b in zip(ids[:-1], ids[1:]):
        precedences.append((a, b))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. SAME‑CENTER PAIRS (resource capacity = 1)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
center_to_ops = {}
for op in ops:
    center_to_ops.setdefault(op["center"], []).append(op["id"])

same_center_pairs = []       # list of unordered pairs (i , j) sharing a center
for lst in center_to_ops.values():
    for i in range(len(lst)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(lst)):
            same_center_pairs.append((lst[i], lst[j]))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. BIG‑M (larger than any feasible makespan)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
M = sum(op["proc"] for op in ops)   # total processing time – safe upper bound

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. MODEL
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("S", [op["id"] for op in ops], lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# binary ordering variables for each pair that shares a center
Y = {}
for (i, j) in same_center_pairs:
    var_name = f"Y_{i}_{j}"
    Y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. OBJECTIVE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. CONSTRAINTS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8.1  Precedence constraints inside each truck
for (i, j) in precedences:
    model += S[j] >= S[i] + ops[i]["proc"], f"Precedence_{i}_before_{j}"

# 8.2  Disjunctive constraints for operations using the same center
for (i, j) in same_center_pairs:
    # i before j  OR  j before i
    model += S[i] + ops[i]["proc"] <= S[j] + M * (1 - Y[(i, j)]), f"Center_{i}_before_{j}"
    model += S[j] + ops[j]["proc"] <= S[i] + M * Y[(i, j)],       f"Center_{j}_before_{i}"

# 8.3  Definition of makespan
for op in ops:
    model += Cmax >= S[op["id"]] + op["proc"], f"Makespan_def_{op['id']}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. SOLVE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. OUTPUT (optional – prints schedule sorted by start time)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if pulp.LpStatus[model.status] == "Optimal":
    schedule = sorted(
        [(op["id"], op["truck"], op["center"], op["proc"], pulp.value(S[op["id"]]))
         for op in ops],
        key=lambda x: x[4]
    )
    print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax):.2f}\n")
    print("OpID  Truck  Center  Proc  Start")
    for oid, tr, cen, p, st in schedule:
        print(f"{oid:4d}   {tr:2d}   {cen:5s}   {p:3d}   {st:6.2f}")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found. Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])

"""
Job‑shop model for the 9 trucks (jobs) and 9 distribution centers (machines).
Each truck follows a fixed sequence of operations; each center can serve only one truck at a time.
The model minimizes the makespan (completion time of the last handling operation).
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mapping of center names to machine indices
center_index = {
    "DC1": 1, "DC2": 2, "DC3": 3, "DC4": 4,
    "DC5": 5, "DC6": 6, "DC7": 7, "DC8": 8, "DC9": 9
}

# Routes: list of (center, processing_time) in the required order for each truck
routes = {
    1: [("DC1", 4), ("DC3", 4), ("DC7", 8), ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 5),
        ("DC6",10), ("DC4", 6), ("DC5", 9), ("DC8", 6)],
    2: [("DC8", 1), ("DC1",10), ("DC2", 9), ("DC7", 2), ("DC6",10),
        ("DC5",10), ("DC9", 7), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8)],
    3: [("DC7",10), ("DC1", 5), ("DC6", 9), ("DC5", 5), ("DC9", 7),
        ("DC3",10), ("DC4", 9), ("DC8", 1), ("DC2", 8)],
    4: [("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 8), ("DC3", 2), ("DC5",10), ("DC8", 5),
        ("DC1", 6), ("DC2", 2), ("DC6", 7), ("DC9", 6)],
    5: [("DC1", 1), ("DC2", 1), ("DC7", 5), ("DC6", 8), ("DC3", 2),
        ("DC9", 9), ("DC5", 1), ("DC4", 8), ("DC8", 4)],
    6: [("DC5", 5), ("DC9", 6), ("DC7", 1), ("DC3",10), ("DC2",10),
        ("DC4",10), ("DC6", 5), ("DC8", 2), ("DC1", 6)],
    7: [("DC2", 9), ("DC3", 8), ("DC4", 8), ("DC7", 5), ("DC8", 8),
        ("DC5", 2), ("DC9", 2), ("DC1", 3), ("DC6", 9)],
    8: [("DC1", 5), ("DC5", 8), ("DC3", 1), ("DC7", 9), ("DC6", 9),
        ("DC9", 5), ("DC2", 6), ("DC8", 5), ("DC4",10)],
    9: [("DC6",10), ("DC2", 5), ("DC7", 5), ("DC3", 8), ("DC1", 1),
        ("DC4", 8), ("DC9", 3), ("DC5", 4), ("DC8", 6)]
}

num_jobs   = len(routes)               # 9 trucks
ops_per_job = len(next(iter(routes.values())))  # 9 operations per truck

# Create a flat list of all operations with identifiers
# op_id = (job, position)  position starts at 0
operations = {}
for j, seq in routes.items():
    for pos, (center, proc) in enumerate(seq):
        operations[(j, pos)] = {
            "machine": center_index[center],
            "proc": proc
        }

# Big‑M: sum of all processing times + 1 (guarantees feasibility)
M = sum(op["proc"] for op in operations.values()) + 1

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = {}
for (j, p) in operations:
    var_name = f"S_{j}_{p}"
    S[(j, p)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of each job must be within makespan
for j in range(1, num_jobs + 1):
    last_pos = ops_per_job - 1
    model += S[(j, last_pos)] + operations[(j, last_pos)]["proc"] <= Cmax, f"Makespan_job_{j}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each job (fixed order)
for j in range(1, num_jobs + 1):
    for p in range(ops_per_job - 1):
        cur = (j, p)
        nxt = (j, p + 1)
        model += S[cur] + operations[cur]["proc"] <= S[nxt], f"Precedence_job{j}_op{p}_to_{p+1}"

# 3) Machine capacity (disjunctive) constraints
# For each machine, enforce that any two operations using it do not overlap.
# Introduce binary variable y_{a,b} = 1 if operation a precedes b.
y = {}   # key = (a,b) where a<b lexicographically

# Helper to create a deterministic ordering of operation identifiers
def op_key(op):
    j, p = op
    return (j, p)

# Build list of operations per machine
ops_on_machine = {m: [] for m in center_index.values()}
for op_id, data in operations.items():
    ops_on_machine[data["machine"]].append(op_id)

# Generate binary variables and constraints for each unordered pair on the same machine
for m, ops in ops_on_machine.items():
    # there are exactly 9 ops per machine (one per truck)
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for k in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            a = ops[i]
            b = ops[k]
            # binary variable y_{a,b}
            y_name = f"y_{a[0]}_{a[1]}_{b[0]}_{b[1]}"
            y[(a, b)] = pulp.LpVariable(y_name, cat="Binary")
            proc_a = operations[a]["proc"]
            proc_b = operations[b]["proc"]
            # a before b
            model += S[a] + proc_a <= S[b] + M * (1 - y[(a, b)]), f"Machine_{m}_order_{a}_before_{b}"
            # b before a
            model += S[b] + proc_b <= S[a] + M * y[(a, b)], f"Machine_{m}_order_{b}_before_{a}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output (optional, for verification)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum makespan (total completion time):", pulp.value(Cmax))

# Print start times in a readable format
for j in range(1, num_jobs + 1):
    print(f"\nTruck {j} schedule:")
    for p in range(ops_per_job):
        op = (j, p)
        start = pulp.value(S[op])
        proc = operations[op]["proc"]
        machine = operations[op]["machine"]
        print(f"  Op {p+1} (Center {machine}) : start = {start:.2f}, duration = {proc}, finish = {start+proc:.2f}")

"""
0‑1 knapsack model for the shipping company problem.
Select a subset of packages to maximize total revenue while keeping total
volume ≤ 234 cubic feet.  Each package is either taken completely (1) or not taken (0).

Solver: HiGHS (via PuLP)
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Package indices (1‑based for readability)
packages = list(range(1, 15))

# Volume (cubic feet) of each package
volume = {
    1: 39,
    2: 29,
    3: 17,
    4: 38,
    5: 25,
    6: 29,
    7: 4,
    8: 6,
    9: 22,
    10: 33,
    11: 3,
    12: 40,
    13: 18,
    14: 32,
}

# Revenue (dollars) of each package
revenue = {
    1: 116,
    2: 217,
    3: 20,
    4: 78,
    5: 97,
    6: 299,
    7: 202,
    8: 217,
    9: 129,
    10: 243,
    11: 255,
    12: 62,
    13: 269,
    14: 292,
}

# Cargo container capacity
capacity = 234

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables: x_i = 1 if package i is shipped, 0 otherwise
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    packages,
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Create a maximization problem

# Objective: maximize total revenue

    "Volume_Limit",
)

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 9 products (jobs) and 9 workstations (machines).
Each product has a fixed sequence of operations (machine, processing time).
The model minimizes the makespan (total completion time) using a
disjunctive formulation with binary ordering variables.
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Routes: list of (machine, processing_time) for each product P1..P9
routes = {
    1: [(5, 7), (3, 7), (7, 7), (2, 1), (4, 3), (6, 10), (1, 5), (8, 5), (9, 1)],
    2: [(4, 4), (5, 10), (9, 10), (7, 1), (1, 2), (3, 6), (8, 8), (2, 4), (6, 5)],
    3: [(5, 8), (2, 9), (7, 7), (1, 9), (6, 8), (4, 3), (9, 3), (8, 1), (3, 9)],
    4: [(8,10), (2, 4), (7, 8), (4, 7), (3, 1), (9, 3), (1, 5), (6, 5), (5, 9)],
    5: [(5, 8), (7, 9), (8, 6), (9, 8), (1,10), (4, 2), (6, 5), (2, 4), (3, 7)],
    6: [(8,10), (6, 4), (4,10), (9, 3), (2, 9), (7, 5), (5, 2), (1, 3), (3, 1)],
    7: [(9, 6), (8, 5), (7, 7), (5, 1), (4, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4), (6, 7), (2, 2)],
    8: [(1, 8), (7,10), (4, 1), (5, 2), (2, 1), (9, 5), (6, 3), (8, 8), (3, 3)],
    9: [(4, 6), (9, 3), (6, 2), (2, 1), (5,10), (1, 1), (8, 1), (7, 4), (3, 7)]
}

# Create a dictionary for every operation (job, op_index) → (machine, proc_time)
ops = {}
for job, seq in routes.items():
    for idx, (machine, proc) in enumerate(seq):
        ops[(job, idx)] = {"machine": machine, "proc": proc}

# Big‑M value – larger than any possible makespan
M = sum(v["proc"] for v in ops.values())   # 421 in this instance

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop_Makespan_Minimisation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("S", ops.keys(), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.1. Job (precedence) constraints
for job in routes.keys():
    num_ops = len(routes[job])
    for k in range(num_ops - 1):
        cur = (job, k)
        nxt = (job, k + 1)
        model += S[cur] + ops[cur]["proc"] <= S[nxt], f"Job{job}_op{k}_to_op{k+1}"

# 4.2. Machine (disjunctive) constraints
#   For every pair of operations that share the same machine we introduce a binary
#   ordering variable.
binary_vars = {}
# Group operations by machine
machine_ops = {}
for key, data in ops.items():
    m = data["machine"]
    machine_ops.setdefault(m, []).append(key)

for m, op_list in machine_ops.items():
    # all unordered pairs on the same machine
    for i in range(len(op_list)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(op_list)):
            op_i = op_list[i]
            op_j = op_list[j]
            y_name = f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
            Y = pulp.LpVariable(y_name, cat="Binary")
            binary_vars[(op_i, op_j)] = Y

            # If Y = 1 → op_i precedes op_j
            model += (
                S[op_i] + ops[op_i]["proc"] <= S[op_j] + M * (1 - Y),
                f"Machine{m}_order_{op_i}_before_{op_j}",
            )
            # If Y = 0 → op_j precedes op_i
            model += (
                S[op_j] + ops[op_j]["proc"] <= S[op_i] + M * Y,
                f"Machine{m}_order_{op_j}_before_{op_i}",
            )

# 4.3. Makespan definition – must be at least the completion time of every job
for job, seq in routes.items():
    last_op = (job, len(seq) - 1)
    model += Cmax >= S[last_op] + ops[last_op]["proc"], f"Makespan_job{job}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Output (optional – printed when script is run)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (rounded):")
for job in sorted(routes.keys()):
    for idx in range(len(routes[job])):
        key = (job, idx)
        st = pulp.value(S[key])
        print(f"  Job {job} Op {idx+1} (Machine {ops[key]['machine']}) : {st:.2f}")

# Big-M: a safe upper bound for any start time difference
bigM = sum(op["proc"] for op in operations.values()) + 1  # +1 for safety

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop_Makespan_Minimization", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous >=0)
start = {}
for op_key in operations:
    start[op_key] = pulp.LpVariable(f"Start_{op_key[0]}_{op_key[1]}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

                f"Machine_{m}_order1_{op_i}_{op_j}"
            )

                start[op_i] >= start[op_j] + operations[op_j]["proc"] - bigM * y[(op_i, op_j)],
                f"Machine_{m}_order2_{op_i}_{op_j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# routes[product] = list of (workstation, processing_time) in order

    1: [(5, 7), (3, 7), (7, 7), (2, 1), (4, 3), (6, 10), (1, 5), (8, 5), (9, 1)],

    4: [(8, 10), (2, 4), (7, 8), (4, 7), (3, 1), (9, 3), (1, 5), (6, 5), (5, 9)],
    5: [(5, 8), (7, 9), (8, 6), (9, 8), (1, 10), (4, 2), (6, 5), (2, 4), (3, 7)],
    6: [(8, 10), (6, 4), (4, 10), (9, 3), (2, 9), (7, 5), (5, 2), (1, 3), (3, 1)],
    7: [(9, 6), (8, 5), (7, 7), (5, 1), (4, 1), (3, 1), (1, 4), (6, 7), (2, 2)],
    8: [(1, 8), (7, 10), (4, 1), (5, 2), (2, 1), (9, 5), (6, 3), (8, 8), (3, 3)],
    9: [(4, 6), (9, 3), (6, 2), (2, 1), (5, 10), (1, 1), (8, 1), (7, 4), (3, 7)]
}

products = list(routes.keys())
num_ops = {p: len(routes[p]) for p in products}

# Helper dictionaries
proc_time = {}   # (product, op_index) -> processing time
machine   = {}   # (product, op_index) -> workstation number
for p, ops in routes.items():
    for idx, (w, t) in enumerate(ops):
        proc_time[(p, idx)] = t
        machine[(p, idx)] = w

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          [(p, o) for p in products for o in range(num_ops[p])],
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
model += Cmax  # objective: minimise makespan

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each product (job)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for p in products:
    for o in range(num_ops[p] - 1):
        model += (S[(p, o + 1)] >= S[(p, o)] + proc_time[(p, o)],
                  f"Precedence_P{p}_O{o}_to_O{o+1}")

for w, ops in ops_on_machine.items():
    # create a binary variable for each unordered pair (i,j)
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            op_i = ops[i]
            op_j = ops[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op_i}_{op_j}"
            Y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")
            # i before j
            model += (S[op_i] + proc_time[op_i] <= S[op_j] + M * (1 - Y[(op_i, op_j)]),
                      f"Machine{w}_order_{op_i}_before_{op_j}")
            # j before i
            model += (S[op_j] + proc_time[op_j] <= S[op_i] + M * Y[(op_i, op_j)],
                      f"Machine{w}_order_{op_j}_before_{op_i}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for p in products:
    last = num_ops[p] - 1
    model += (Cmax >= S[(p, last)] + proc_time[(p, last)],
              f"Makespan_def_P{p}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (rounded to 2 decimals):")
for p in sorted(products):
    print(f"Product {p}:")
    for o in range(num_ops[p]):
        start = pulp.value(S[(p, o)])
        w = machine[(p, o)]
        t = proc_time[(p, o)]
        print(f"  Op {o+1} (W{w}, t={t}) -> start = {start:.2f}")
    print()
