# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Traveling Salesman Problem for 4 facilities (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta)

The technician must start at Alpha, visit each facility exactly once,
and return to Alpha while minimizing total travel time.
"""

import pulp

# -----------------------------
# Data
# -----------------------------
nodes = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta"]
n = len(nodes)

# Travel times (minutes) – symmetric matrix
travel_time = {
    ("Alpha", "Beta"): 129.2,
    ("Alpha", "Gamma"): 46.6,
    ("Alpha", "Delta"): 139.6,
    ("Beta", "Gamma"): 86.3,
    ("Beta", "Delta"): 58.3,
    ("Gamma", "Delta"): 110.3,
}
# Fill the symmetric entries
for i, j in list(travel_time.keys()):
    travel_time[(j, i)] = travel_time[(i, j)]

# -----------------------------
# Model
# -----------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i,j] == 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j, 0 otherwise (binary)
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# MTZ order variables (continuous)
# u[i] gives the position of node i in the tour (except the start node)
u = {}
for i in nodes:
    if i == "Alpha":  # start node fixed at position 0
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=0, upBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)
    else:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(
            f"u_{i}", lowBound=1, upBound=n - 1, cat=pulp.LpContinuous
        )

# Objective: minimise total travel time
model += pulp.lpSum(travel_time[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in x), "Total_Travel_Time"

# Constraints
# 1) Exactly one outgoing arc from each node
for i in nodes:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1,
        f"One_out_of_{i}",
    )

# 2) Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in nodes:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
        f"One_into_{j}",
    )

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j and i != "Alpha" and j != "Alpha":
            model += (
                u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1,
                f"MTZ_{i}_{j}",
            )

# -----------------------------
# Solve
# -----------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# -----------------------------
# Output
# -----------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    # Extract the tour arcs
    tour_arcs = [(i, j) for (i, j) in x if pulp.value(x[(i, j)]) > 0.5]

    # Build ordered tour starting from Alpha
    tour = ["Alpha"]
    while len(tour) < n + 1:  # +1 to return to start
        last = tour[-1]
        # find the next node
        next_node = next(j for (i, j) in tour_arcs if i == last)
        tour.append(next_node)

    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print("Optimal tour (in order):")
    print(" -> ".join(tour))
    print(f"Total travel time: {total_time:.1f} minutes")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

Traveling Salesman Problem for 4 regional facilities.
The script builds a MILP model with PuLP (HiGHS solver) and prints the optimal tour
and its total travel time.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
facilities = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta"]          # nodes
n = len(facilities)

# travel times (minutes) – symmetric distances
travel = {
    ("Alpha", "Beta"):   129.2,
    ("Alpha", "Gamma"):   46.6,
    ("Alpha", "Delta"):  139.6,
    ("Beta",  "Gamma"):   86.3,
    ("Beta",  "Delta"):   58.3,
    ("Gamma", "Delta"):  110.3,
}
# make the matrix symmetric
for i, j in list(travel.keys()):
    travel[(j, i)] = travel[(i, j)]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Facility_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if we travel directly from i to j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in facilities for j in facilities if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# MTZ order variables (continuous)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "u",
    facilities,
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=n,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in x), "Total_Travel_Time"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Exactly one outgoing edge from each facility
for i in facilities:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in facilities if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{i}"

# 2) Exactly one incoming edge to each facility
for j in facilities:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in facilities if i != j) == 1, f"In_{j}"

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination
# Fix the order of the start node (Alpha) to 1
model += u["Alpha"] == 1, "Start_order"

# Remaining nodes must have order values between 2 and n
for i in facilities:
    if i != "Alpha":
        model += u[i] >= 2, f"OrderLow_{i}"
        model += u[i] <= n, f"OrderHigh_{i}"

# MTZ constraints for all i != j, i,j != Alpha (the start node)
for i in facilities:
    for j in facilities:
        if i != j and i != "Alpha" and j != "Alpha":
            model += (
                u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1,
                f"MTZ_{i}_{j}",
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes\n")

    # Reconstruct the tour
    tour = []
    current = "Alpha"
    while True:
        tour.append(current)
        # find the successor of the current node
        next_node = None
        for j in facilities:
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:
                next_node = j
                break
        if next_node is None or next_node == "Alpha":
            break
        current = next_node

    tour.append("Alpha")  # return to start
    print("Optimal tour:")
    print(" -> ".join(tour))
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

"""
Traveling Salesperson Problem for 8 corporate offices.
The goal is to find the minimum‑time tour that starts at an office,
visits each office exactly once and returns to the start.

The model uses:
  - binary decision variables x[i][j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j
  - continuous MTZ variables u[i] to eliminate subtours
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
offices = [
    "Alpha",   # 0
    "Beta",    # 1
    "Gamma",   # 2
    "Delta",   # 3
    "Epsilon", # 4
    "Zeta",    # 5
    "Eta",     # 6
    "Theta",   # 7
]

# Travel times (minutes) – symmetric matrix, diagonal = 0
# rows/cols follow the order of the list above
travel = [
    # A      B      G      D      E      Z      H      T
    [0.0, 177.3,  32.4,  30.7, 119.9, 141.7, 158.8, 108.7],  # Alpha
    [177.3, 0.0, 150.7, 190.7,  83.4, 184.9,  73.9, 184.9],  # Beta
    [32.4, 150.7, 0.0,  40.5,  87.9, 151.5, 143.3, 122.6],   # Gamma
    [30.7, 190.7, 40.5, 0.0, 122.4, 172.4, 182.1, 139.1],    # Delta
    [119.9, 83.4, 87.9, 122.4, 0.0, 191.6, 120.0, 175.7],    # Epsilon
    [141.7, 184.9,151.5,172.4,191.6, 0.0, 116.5,  36.0],    # Zeta
    [158.8, 73.9,143.3,182.1,120.0,116.5, 0.0, 125.2],      # Eta
    [108.7,184.9,122.6,139.1,175.7, 36.0,125.2, 0.0],       # Theta
]

N = len(offices)                     # number of nodes (8)
nodes = range(N)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Corporate_Office_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# 2.1 Decision variables: x[i][j] binary, i != j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# 2.2 MTZ auxiliary variables u[i] (continuous), only for i != 0 (depot)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "u",
    (i for i in nodes if i != 0),
    lowBound=1,
    upBound=N - 1,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Objective: minimise total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel[i][j] * x[(i, j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.1 Exactly one outgoing edge from each node
for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"out_{i}"

# 4.2 Exactly one incoming edge to each node
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"in_{j}"

# 4.3 MTZ subtour elimination constraints
#    u_i - u_j + N * x_ij <= N-1   for i != j, i != 0, j != 0
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j and i != 0 and j != 0:
            model += (
                u[i] - u[j] + N * x[(i, j)] <= N - 1,
                f"mtz_{i}_{j}",
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal" or status == "Feasible":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes\n")

    # Build the tour order
    # start from node 0 (Alpha)
    current = 0
    tour = [offices[current]]
    visited = {current}
    while len(tour) < N:
        # find j such that x[current, j] == 1
        next_node = None
        for j in nodes:
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:
                next_node = j
                break
        if next_node is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Failed to reconstruct tour.")
        tour.append(offices[next_node])
        visited.add(next_node)
        current = next_node

    # return to start
    tour.append(offices[0])

    print("Optimal tour:")
    print(" -> ".join(tour))
else:
    print("No feasible solution found.")

]

            x[i, j] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

"""
Traveling Salesman Problem for 11 remote sensor stations.
The technician must start at Alpha, visit every station exactly once,
and return to Alpha while minimizing total travel time.

Model: MTZ (Miller‑Tucker‑Zemlin) formulation.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
stations = [
    "Alpha",   # 0
    "Bravo",   # 1
    "Charlie", # 2
    "Delta",   # 3
    "Echo",    # 4
    "Foxtrot", # 5
    "Golf",    # 6
    "Hotel",   # 7
    "India",   # 8
    "Juliet",  # 9
    "Kilo"     #10
]

# pairwise travel times (minutes) – symmetric
raw_times = {
    ("Alpha","Bravo"):   85.0,
    ("Alpha","Charlie"):117.4,
    ("Alpha","Delta"):   68.8,
    ("Alpha","Echo"):    76.6,
    ("Alpha","Foxtrot"):139.0,
    ("Alpha","Golf"):   104.7,
    ("Alpha","Hotel"):   54.5,
    ("Alpha","India"):   83.8,
    ("Alpha","Juliet"):  64.3,
    ("Alpha","Kilo"):    77.0,
    ("Bravo","Charlie"):123.0,
    ("Bravo","Delta"):  139.3,
    ("Bravo","Echo"):    75.5,
    ("Bravo","Foxtrot"):113.2,
    ("Bravo","Golf"):   175.0,
    ("Bravo","Hotel"):   58.4,
    ("Bravo","India"):  166.0,
    ("Bravo","Juliet"): 149.2,
    ("Bravo","Kilo"):   154.0,
    ("Charlie","Delta"): 98.2,
    ("Charlie","Echo"): 175.5,
    ("Charlie","Foxtrot"):46.0,
    ("Charlie","Golf"): 114.2,
    ("Charlie","Hotel"): 75.3,
    ("Charlie","India"):139.8,

    ("Charlie","Kilo"): 185.1,
    ("Delta","Echo"):   145.2,
    ("Delta","Foxtrot"):138.2,
    ("Delta","Golf"):    36.6,
    ("Delta","Hotel"):   85.2,
    ("Delta","India"):   41.6,
    ("Delta","Juliet"):  61.0,
    ("Delta","Kilo"):   100.3,
    ("Echo","Foxtrot"): 180.0,
    ("Echo","Golf"):    180.6,
    ("Echo","Hotel"):   100.2,
    ("Echo","India"):   153.2,
    ("Echo","Juliet"):  122.5,
    ("Echo","Kilo"):    107.1,
    ("Foxtrot","Golf"): 158.7,
    ("Foxtrot","Hotel"): 86.3,
    ("Foxtrot","India"):179.5,
    ("Foxtrot","Juliet"):186.6,
    ("Foxtrot","Kilo"): 213.5,
    ("Golf","Hotel"):   119.3,
    ("Golf","India"):    45.2,
    ("Golf","Juliet"):   79.8,
    ("Golf","Kilo"):    120.8,
    ("Hotel","India"):  118.4,
    ("Hotel","Juliet"): 112.0,
    ("Hotel","Kilo"):   131.2,
    ("India","Juliet"):  37.2,
    ("India","Kilo"):    77.1,
    ("Juliet","Kilo"):   41.1
}

# Build a complete symmetric distance dictionary
dist = {}
for (i, j), v in raw_times.items():
    dist[(i, j)] = v
    dist[(j, i)] = v

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
n = len(stations)
idx = range(n)

model = pulp.LpProblem("Sensor_Station_Calibration_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: x[i][j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x", (idx, idx), lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# MTZ order variables (continuous)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("u", idx, lowBound=0, upBound=n-1, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(dist[(stations[i], stations[j])] * x[i][j]
                   for i in idx for j in idx if i != j), "TotalTravelTime"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Exactly one outgoing arc from each node
for i in idx:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i][j] for j in idx if j != i) == 1, f"Out_{stations[i]}"

# 2) Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in idx:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i][j] for i in idx if i != j) == 1, f"In_{stations[j]}"

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination
# Fix the order of the depot (Alpha) to 0
model += u[0] == 0, "DepotOrder"

for i in idx:
    if i == 0:
        continue
    # u_i must be between 1 and n-1
    model += u[i] >= 1, f"OrderLow_{stations[i]}"
    model += u[i] <= n-1, f"OrderHigh_{stations[i]}"

for i in idx:
    for j in idx:
        if i == j or i == 0 or j == 0:
            continue
        # u_i - u_j + (n-1)*x_ij <= n-2
        model += u[i] - u[j] + (n-1) * x[i][j] <= n-2, f"MTZ_{stations[i]}_{stations[j]}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Total travel time = {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f} minutes\n")

# Reconstruct the tour
tour = []
current = 0  # start at Alpha (index 0)
while True:
    tour.append(current)
    # find the next node j with x[current][j] == 1
    next_node = None
    for j in idx:
        if j != current and pulp.value(x[current][j]) > 0.5:
            next_node = j
            break
    if next_node is None or next_node == 0:
        break
    current = next_node

# Append return to depot
tour.append(0)

# Print readable tour
readable_tour = " -> ".join(stations[i] for i in tour)
print("Optimal calibration circuit:")
print(readable_tour)

The technician must start at a station, visit every other station exactly once,
and return to the start while minimizing total travel time.

x = {}

for 7 branch offices using PuLP and the HiGHS solver.

3 – Delta
4 – Epsilon

6 – Eta

# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
offices = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon", "Zeta", "Eta"]
n = len(offices)                     # number of nodes

# travel times (minutes) – symmetric matrix, only upper‑triangle given
travel = {
    (0, 1): 89.9,
    (0, 2): 120.1,
    (0, 3): 72.2,
    (0, 4): 87.3,
    (0, 5): 56.0,
    (0, 6): 78.2,
    (1, 2): 162.9,
    (1, 3): 45.9,
    (1, 4): 96.0,

    (2, 6): 186.9,
    (3, 4): 50.2,
    (3, 5): 116.3,
    (3, 6): 145.2,
    (4, 5): 142.1,
    (4, 6): 165.4,
    (5, 6): 32.0,
}

# Complete the symmetric matrix
dist = {}
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        if i == j:
            dist[i, j] = 0.0
        elif (i, j) in travel:
            dist[i, j] = travel[i, j]
        elif (j, i) in travel:
            dist[i, j] = travel[j, i]
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing travel time for pair ({i},{j})")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Branch_Visit_Itinerary", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
# x[i][j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j, 0 otherwise (binary)
x = {}
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        if i != j:
            var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
            x[i, j] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# MTZ auxiliary variables to eliminate subtours:
# u[i] is the position of node i in the tour (continuous)
u = {}
for i in range(n):
    # Alpha (node 0) is the depot; fix its order to 0
    if i == 0:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=0, upBound=0, cat="Continuous")
    else:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=1, upBound=n - 1, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

for i in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"out_{i}"

# 2) Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"in_{j}"

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination constraints
#    u_i - u_j + n * x_ij <= n - 1   for all i != j, i != 0, j != 0
M = n
for i in range(1, n):
    for j in range(1, n):
        if i != j:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + M * x[i, j] <= M - 1, f"mtz_{i}_{j}"

# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]

    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.1f} minutes")

    # Reconstruct the tour starting from Alpha (node 0)
    tour = [0]
    while len(tour) < n + 1:   # +1 to return to start
        last = tour[-1]
        # find the node j such that x_last_j == 1
        next_node = None
        for j in range(n):
            if last != j and pulp.value(x[last, j]) > 0.5:

    named_tour = [offices[i] for i in tour]
    print("Optimal visit order:")
    print(" -> ".join(named_tour))
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

import pulp

# Data
# -----------------------------
nodes = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon", "Zeta", "Eta"]

    ("Delta", "Epsilon"): 50.2,
    ("Delta", "Zeta"): 116.3,
    ("Delta", "Eta"): 145.2,
    ("Epsilon", "Zeta"): 142.1,
    ("Epsilon", "Eta"): 165.4,
    ("Zeta", "Eta"): 32.0,
}

# make the matrix symmetric
for (i, j), d in list(dist.items()):
    dist[(j, i)] = d

# -----------------------------
# Model
# -----------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Branch_Visit_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# binary decision variables: 1 if travel directly from i to j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# MTZ auxiliary variables (continuous)
# u[Alpha] is fixed to 1, others are in [2, N]
u = {}
for i in nodes:
    if i == "Alpha":
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=1, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)
    else:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=2, upBound=N, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Objective: minimise total travel time
model += pulp.lpSum(dist[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)

# Each node has exactly one outgoing arc
for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"out_{i}"

# Each node has exactly one incoming arc
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"in_{j}"

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j and i != "Alpha" and j != "Alpha":
            model += (
                u[i] - u[j] + N * x[(i, j)] <= N - 1,
                f"mtz_{i}_{j}",

# Solve
# -----------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# Output
# -----------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]

    tour = {}
    for (i, j), var in x.items():
        if var.value() > 0.5:
            tour[i] = j

    # reconstruct ordered route starting at Alpha
    route = ["Alpha"]
    while True:
        nxt = tour[route[-1]]

            break
        route.append(nxt)

    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print("Optimal route:")
    print(" -> ".join(route))
    print(f"Total travel time: {total_time:.1f} minutes")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"In_{j}"

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination

    (2, 5): 105.2,  (5, 2): 105.2,

    (3, 5): 135.7,  (5, 3): 135.7,
    (4, 5): 185.4,  (5, 4): 185.4,
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Branch_Visit_Itinerary", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: x[i][j] = 1 if travel directly from i to j, 0 otherwise
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x", [(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j],
                          lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# MTZ ordering variables (continuous, used to eliminate subtours)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("u", nodes, lowBound=1, upBound=len(nodes), cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total travel time
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel_time[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)

    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"out_{i}"

# 2) Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"in_{j}"

# Reconstruct the full route starting from node 1

    (3, 5): 135.7, (5, 3): 135.7,
    (4, 5): 185.4, (5, 4): 185.4,
}

# Model
# -------------------------------------------------

# Binary decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if travel directly from i to j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

    "u",
    (i for i in nodes),
    lowBound=1,
    upBound=len(nodes),
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{i}"

for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"In_{j}"

        if next_node is None or next_node == 1:

"""
Traveling Salesperson Problem for 5 corporate offices.
The script builds a MILP model with PuLP and solves it using HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
offices = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon"]
n = len(offices)

# travel times (minutes) – symmetric matrix, 0 on the diagonal
travel = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]

# fill the upper triangle from the statement
travel[0][1] = 156.8   # Alpha‑Beta
travel[0][2] = 226.4   # Alpha‑Gamma
travel[0][3] = 151.3   # Alpha‑Delta
travel[0][4] = 173.9   # Alpha‑Epsilon

travel[1][2] = 171.0   # Beta‑Gamma
travel[1][3] = 192.9   # Beta‑Delta
travel[1][4] = 181.9   # Beta‑Epsilon

travel[2][3] = 118.1   # Gamma‑Delta
travel[2][4] = 80.0    # Gamma‑Epsilon

travel[3][4] = 38.5    # Delta‑Epsilon

# copy to lower triangle to make the matrix symmetric
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i + 1, n):
        travel[j][i] = travel[i][j]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Office_Visit_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
# x[i][j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j, 0 otherwise (binary)
x = {}
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        if i != j:
            var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
            x[i, j] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# u[i] – auxiliary ordering variables for MTZ subtour elimination (continuous)
# u[0] is fixed to 1 (the start node). For the remaining nodes 2..n
u = {}
for i in range(n):
    if i == 0:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=1, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)
    else:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=2, upBound=n, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j), "Total_Travel_Time"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Exactly one outgoing edge from each node
for i in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"OutDeg_{i}"

# 2. Exactly one incoming edge to each node
for j in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"InDeg_{j}"

# 3. MTZ subtour elimination constraints
#    u_i - u_j + n * x_ij <= n - 1   for all i != j, i != 0, j != 0
for i in range(1, n):
    for j in range(1, n):
        if i != j:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1, f"MTZ_{i}_{j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes\n")

    # Reconstruct the tour
    tour = []
    current = 0  # start at Alpha (index 0)
    visited = set()
    while True:
        tour.append(current)
        visited.add(current)
        # find the next node
        next_node = None
        for j in range(n):
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[current, j]) > 0.5:
                next_node = j
                break
        if next_node is None or next_node == 0:
            break
        current = next_node
        if len(visited) == n:
            # close the loop back to the start
            tour.append(0)
            break

    # Print readable itinerary
    readable = " -> ".join(offices[i] for i in tour)
    print("Optimal itinerary:")
    print(readable)
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

travel[2][4] = travel[4][2] = 80.0    # Gamma–Epsilon

travel[3][4] = travel[4][3] = 38.5    # Delta–Epsilon

x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in offices for j in offices if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

    "u",
    (i for i in offices if i != 0),
    lowBound=2,
    upBound=n,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# 3. Objective: minimise total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel[i][j] * x[(i, j)] for i in offices for j in offices if i != j)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Constraints

for i in offices:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in offices if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{i}"

for j in offices:

        for j in offices:

                break
        if next_node is None or next_node == 0:

        tour.append(next_node)

y = {}
for (i, j), cost in edge_data.items():
    var_name = f"y_{i}_{j}"
    y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat="Binary")

# Continuous flow variables: f[i,j] (directional) for each existing edge
f = {}
for (i, j), cost in edge_data.items():
    f[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"f_{i}_{j}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
    f[(j, i)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"f_{j}_{i}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(cost * y[(i, j)] for (i, j), cost in edge_data.items()), "Total_Latency"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Exactly n-1 edges must be chosen (property of a spanning tree)
model += pulp.lpSum(y[(i, j)] for (i, j) in y) == n - 1, "Tree_Edge_Count"

# 2) Flow conservation constraints (root supplies n‑1 units, each other node consumes 1)
for node in nodes:
    inflow = pulp.lpSum(f[(i, node)] for (i, j) in edge_data if j == node) + \
             pulp.lpSum(f[(j, node)] for (i, j) in edge_data if i == node)
    outflow = pulp.lpSum(f[(node, j)] for (i, j) in edge_data if i == node) + \
              pulp.lpSum(f[(node, i)] for (i, j) in edge_data if j == node)

    ("Q", "U"): 117.2,
    ("Q", "V"): 78.6,
    ("Q", "W"): 32.3,
}

# Ensure each edge is stored with the smaller node first (canonical ordering)
edge_latency = {tuple(sorted(k)): v for k, v in edge_latency.items()}

# -------------------------
# Model
# -------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Minimum_Latency_Spanning_Tree", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Binary decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if edge (i,j) is selected
x = {}
for (i, j) in edge_latency:
    var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
    x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# Continuous flow variables (directed) to enforce connectivity
# f[i,j] is the amount of flow sent from i to j through edge (i,j)
f = {}
bigM = len(nodes) - 1  # maximum possible flow on any edge
for (i, j) in edge_latency:
    f[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"f_{i}_{j}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
    f[(j, i)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"f_{j}_{i}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# -------------------------
# Objective: minimise total latency of selected edges
# -------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(edge_latency[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in edge_latency), "Total_Latency"

# -------------------------
# Constraints
# -------------------------

# 1) Exactly (n-1) edges must be selected (property of a spanning tree)
model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in edge_latency) == len(nodes) - 1, "Tree_Edge_Count"

# 2) Flow conservation (single‑commodity flow formulation)
root = "P"  # choose P as the root of the tree

# Supply at root: it must emit (n‑1) units of flow
model += (
    pulp.lpSum(f[(root, j)] for j in nodes if (root, j) in f) -
    pulp.lpSum(f[(i, root)] for i in nodes if (i, root) in f) == len(nodes) - 1,
    "Root_Supply",
)

# Demand at every other node: each must receive exactly 1 unit of flow
for node in nodes:
    if node == root:
        continue
    inflow = pulp.lpSum(f[(i, node)] for i in nodes if (i, node) in f)
    outflow = pulp.lpSum(f[(node, j)] for j in nodes if (node, j) in f)
    model += inflow - outflow == 1, f"Demand_{node}"

# 3) Capacity linking flow and edge‑selection
# If an edge is not chosen, no flow may traverse it.
for (i, j) in edge_latency:
    model += f[(i, j)] <= bigM * x[(i, j)], f"Cap_{i}_{j}_forward"
    model += f[(j, i)] <= bigM * x[(i, j)], f"Cap_{i}_{j}_backward"

# -------------------------
# Solve
# -------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# -------------------------
# Output results
# -------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    total_latency = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Total latency of the spanning tree: {total_latency:.2f} ms")
    print("Selected edges:")
    for (i, j), var in x.items():

            print(f"  {i} – {j}  (latency = {edge_latency[(i, j)]} ms)")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

The technician must be able to reach all eight network nodes.

of the selected links.

The data are the pairwise latencies (in ms) given in the statement.

# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

root = "P"                       # we root the tree at node P
n = len(nodes)

latency = {
    ("P", "Q"): 104.0,

    ("P", "S"): 114.8,
    ("P", "T"): 129.1,
    ("P", "U"): 14.6,
    ("P", "V"): 87.0,
    ("P", "W"): 76.6,
    ("Q", "R"): 78.4,
    ("Q", "S"): 98.2,
    ("Q", "T"): 92.5,
    ("Q", "U"): 117.2,
    ("Q", "V"): 78.6,
    ("Q", "W"): 32.3,
}

# Because latency is symmetric, add the reverse direction
for (i, j), d in list(latency.items()):
    latency[(j, i)] = d

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Dispatch_MinLatencyTree", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
# x[i,j] = 1 if the (directed) arc i→j is used in the spanning tree
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x",
                          [(i, j) for (i, j) in latency.keys()],
                          lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# u[i] = position of node i in the MTZ ordering (root has 0)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("u", nodes, lowBound=0, upBound=n-1, cat=pulp.LpInteger)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total latency of the selected (undirected) edges
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(latency[i, j] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in latency.keys()), "TotalLatency"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Exactly one incoming arc for every node except the root
for v in nodes:
    if v == root:
        # root receives no incoming arc
        model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, v)] for i in nodes if (i, v) in x) == 0, f"Incoming_{v}"
    else:
        model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, v)] for i in nodes if (i, v) in x) == 1, f"Incoming_{v}"

# 2) The total number of selected arcs must be (n‑1)
model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in x) == n - 1, "ArcCount"

# 3) MTZ subtour‑elimination constraints
#    u[root] is fixed to 0
model += u[root] == 0, "RootOrder"

All missing latencies are assigned a very large value so that the optimal
tour will use only the listed (real) edges whenever possible.

    ("Q", "S"): 98.2,
    ("Q", "T"): 92.5,
    ("Q", "U"): 117.2,
    ("Q", "V"): 78.6,
    ("Q", "W"): 32.3,
}

# make the matrix symmetric and fill missing entries with a huge penalty
BIG = 1e6  # penalty for non‑existent edges
dist = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i == j:
            dist[(i, j)] = 0.0
        elif (i, j) in latency:
            dist[(i, j)] = latency[(i, j)]
        elif (j, i) in latency:
            dist[(i, j)] = latency[(j, i)]
        else:
            dist[(i, j)] = BIG

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model

model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Dispatch_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "u",
    (i for i in nodes if i != depot),
    lowBound=1,
    upBound=n - 1,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

for i in nodes:

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Minimum‑latency network inspection routing (minimum spanning tree) for 8 nodes.
The technician must be able to reach every node; we model this as a minimum
spanning tree anchored at node P.

Data (latency in ms) – undirected edges:
    P‑Q 104.0   P‑R 26.9   P‑S 114.8  P‑T 129.1  P‑U 14.6  P‑V 87.0  P‑W 76.6
    Q‑R 78.4   Q‑S 98.2   Q‑T 92.5   Q‑U 117.2  Q‑V 78.6  Q‑W 32.3
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Problem definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("NetworkInspection_MST", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Sets
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
nodes = ["P", "Q", "R", "S", "T", "U", "V", "W"]
root = "P"                     # anchoring node for the flow formulation
n = len(nodes)                # number of nodes

# Edge list (undirected) with associated latency cost
edge_data = [
    ("P", "Q", 104.0),
    ("P", "R", 26.9),
    ("P", "S", 114.8),
    ("P", "T", 129.1),
    ("P", "U", 14.6),
    ("P", "V", 87.0),
    ("P", "W", 76.6),
    ("Q", "R", 78.4),
    ("Q", "S", 98.2),
    ("Q", "T", 92.5),
    ("Q", "U", 117.2),
    ("Q", "V", 78.6),
    ("Q", "W", 32.3),
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# x[(i,j)] = 1 if edge (i,j) is selected in the spanning tree, else 0
x = {}
for i, j, _ in edge_data:
    var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
    x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# f[(i,j)] = amount of flow sent on the directed arc i→j (continuous, ≥0)
# The flow formulation guarantees connectivity and eliminates cycles.
f = {}
for i, j, _ in edge_data:
    # two directed arcs for each undirected edge
    f[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"f_{i}_{j}", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)
    f[(j, i)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"f_{j}_{i}", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Objective function
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(cost * x[(i, j)] for i, j, cost in edge_data), "Total_Latency"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.1 Capacity constraints: flow on an arc cannot exceed (n‑1) if the edge is chosen
M = n - 1  # maximum possible flow on any edge
for i, j, _ in edge_data:
    # both directions share the same x‑variable
    model += f[(i, j)] <= M * x[(i, j)], f"Cap_{i}_{j}_forward"
    model += f[(j, i)] <= M * x[(i, j)], f"Cap_{i}_{j}_backward"

# 5.2 Flow conservation
#   - Root node supplies (n‑1) units of flow
#   - Every other node consumes exactly 1 unit
for node in nodes:
    inflow = pulp.lpSum(f[(i, node)] for i, j, _ in edge_data if j == node) + \
             pulp.lpSum(f[(i, node)] for i, j, _ in edge_data if i == node and (i, node) in f)
    outflow = pulp.lpSum(f[(node, j)] for i, j, _ in edge_data if i == node) + \
              pulp.lpSum(f[(node, j)] for i, j, _ in edge_data if j == node and (node, j) in f)

    if node == root:
        model += outflow - inflow == n - 1, f"FlowRoot_{node}"
    else:
        model += inflow - outflow == 1, f"FlowCons_{node}"

# 5.3 (Optional) Eliminate isolated sub‑trees – already guaranteed by flow formulation

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum total latency (ms):", pulp.value(model.objective))

print("\nSelected edges in the minimum‑latency spanning tree:")
for (i, j), var in x.items():
    if pulp.value(var) > 0.5:               # binary variable, treat >0.5 as selected
        # retrieve the cost for printing
        cost = next(c for a, b, c in edge_data if (a == i and b == j) or (a == j and b == i))
        print(f"  {i} – {j} : {cost} ms")

    ("Q", "S"): 104.3,
    ("R", "S"): 21.8,
}

# Complete matrix (symmetric, zero on diagonal)
dist = {}
for i in facilities:
    for j in facilities:
        if i == j:
            dist[(i, j)] = 0.0
        elif (i, j) in travel_time:
            dist[(i, j)] = travel_time[(i, j)]
        elif (j, i) in travel_time:
            dist[(i, j)] = travel_time[(j, i)]
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing travel time for pair ({i},{j})")

# Model
# -------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

idx = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)}  # name → index map

#   rows/columns are ordered as P,Q,R,S

travel[idx["P"]][idx["R"]] = travel[idx["R"]][idx["P"]] = 68.9
travel[idx["P"]][idx["S"]] = travel[idx["S"]][idx["P"]] = 86.4
travel[idx["Q"]][idx["R"]] = travel[idx["R"]][idx["Q"]] = 119.6
travel[idx["Q"]][idx["S"]] = travel[idx["S"]][idx["Q"]] = 104.3
travel[idx["R"]][idx["S"]] = travel[idx["S"]][idx["R"]] = 21.8

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# x[i][j] = 1 if the technician travels directly from i to j, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

)

# 3.2 Each node has exactly one outgoing arc
for i in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{nodes[i]}"

# 3.3 Each node has exactly one incoming arc
for j in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"In_{nodes[j]}"

        # MTZ constraint

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Output

# Reconstruct the tour starting from the depot (P)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    ("Q", "R"): 119.6,
    ("Q", "S"): 104.3,
    ("R", "S"): 21.8,
}
# Complete the symmetric matrix
for i in facilities:
    for j in facilities:
        if i == j:
            travel_time[(i, j)] = 0.0
        elif (i, j) not in travel_time:
            travel_time[(i, j)] = travel_time[(j, i)]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Routing", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: x[i,j] ∈ {0,1} for i ≠ j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in facilities for j in facilities if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

    lowBound=0,

)

    for j in facilities:

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) for 16 facilities.
The goal is to find the minimum‑time Hamiltonian cycle that visits every facility exactly once
and returns to the start node.

Formulation:
    • Binary decision variables x[i,j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j (i≠j), 0 otherwise.
    • Continuous order variables u[i] (i = 1..16) for the Miller‑Tucker‑Zemlin (MTZ) subtour‑elimination.
    • Objective: minimise Σ d[i,j] * x[i,j].
    • Constraints:
        – Each node has exactly one outgoing arc: Σ_{j≠i} x[i,j] = 1   ∀ i
        – Each node has exactly one incoming arc: Σ_{j≠i} x[j,i] = 1   ∀ i
        – MTZ subtour constraints: u[i] - u[j] + N·x[i,j] ≤ N‑1   ∀ i≠j, i≠1, j≠1
        – Fix the order of the start node: u[1] = 1
        – Bounds for order variables: 2 ≤ u[i] ≤ N   ∀ i≠1
All x‑variables are binary; all u‑variables are continuous.

The model is solved with PuLP + HiGHS (max 120 seconds).
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
N = 16                                   # number of facilities
nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

# symmetric travel times (minutes). Only the upper‑triangle is listed in the statement;
# we fill both directions.
dist = {}

# Helper to add both (i,j) and (j,i)
def add(i, j, d):
    dist[(i, j)] = d

    [23.5, 94.2, 102.1, 0.0, 133.7,  44.7],    # Delta
    [113.3,77.2,114.5,133.7, 0.0, 158.1],      # Epsilon
    [49.8, 97.9, 88.1, 44.7, 158.1, 0.0]       # Zeta
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
# x[i][j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j, 0 otherwise
x = {}
for i in range(N):
    for j in range(N):
        if i != j:
            var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
            x[i, j] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

u = {}
for i in range(1, N):
    var_name = f"u_{i}"
    # u_i can take values 2 .. N (inclusive). 1 is reserved for the depot.
    u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=2, upBound=N, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Objective: minimise total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel[i][j] * x[i, j] for i in range(N) for j in range(N) if i != j)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.1. Exactly one outgoing arc from each node
for i in range(N):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in range(N) if i != j) == 1, f"out_{i}"

# 4.2. Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in range(N):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in range(N) if i != j) == 1, f"in_{j}"

# 4.3. MTZ subtour elimination constraints
#    For all i != j, i,j != depot (node 0)
for i in range(1, N):
    for j in range(1, N):
        if i != j:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + N * x[i, j] <= N - 1, f"mtz_{i}_{j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes\n")

    # Reconstruct the tour
    tour = []
    current = 0  # start at depot (Alpha)
    visited = set()
    while True:
        tour.append(current)
        visited.add(current)
        # find the next node where x[current,next] == 1
        next_node = None
        for j in range(N):
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[current, j]) > 0.5:
                next_node = j

        if next_node is None or next_node == 0:

        current = next_node
        if current in visited:
            # safety break to avoid infinite loops if something went wrong

    # Append return to depot
    tour.append(0)

    # Print readable route
    readable_route = " -> ".join(node_names[i] for i in tour)
    print("Optimal tour:")

"""
Traveling Salesman Problem for a 6‑node logistics tour.
The script builds a MILP model with binary arc variables and MTZ subtour
elimination, solves it with PuLP + HiGHS, and prints the optimal circuit
and its total travel time.
"""

import pulp

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
nodes = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon", "Zeta"]
n = len(nodes)

# travel times (minutes) – symmetric, so both directions have the same cost
cost = {
    ("Alpha", "Beta"):    209.8,
    ("Alpha", "Gamma"):   109.1,
    ("Alpha", "Delta"):    23.4,
    ("Alpha", "Epsilon"): 107.3,
    ("Alpha", "Zeta"):     97.2,
    ("Beta", "Gamma"):    198.4,
    ("Beta", "Delta"):    214.1,
    ("Beta", "Epsilon"):  118.8,
    ("Beta", "Zeta"):     216.8,
    ("Gamma", "Delta"):    89.3,
    ("Gamma", "Epsilon"): 155.6,
    ("Gamma", "Zeta"):     24.7,
    ("Delta", "Epsilon"): 120.9,
    ("Delta", "Zeta"):     75.1,
    ("Epsilon", "Zeta"):  161.3,
}

# make the dictionary complete for the directed graph (i -> j)
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i == j:
            continue
        if (i, j) not in cost:
            if (j, i) in cost:
                cost[(i, j)] = cost[(j, i)]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

# 1. Binary decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x", [(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j],
                          lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# 2. MTZ auxiliary variables (continuous) to eliminate subtours
#    u[origin] is fixed to 1, others are in [2, n]
origin = "Alpha"
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("u", [i for i in nodes if i != origin],
                          lowBound=2, upBound=n, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total travel time
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in x), "Total_Travel_Time"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# (a) Exactly one outgoing arc from each node
for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{i}"

# (b) Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"In_{j}"

# (c) MTZ subtour elimination constraints
#     u_i - u_j + n * x_ij <= n-1   for all i != j, i!=origin, j!=origin
for i in nodes:
    if i == origin:
        continue
    for j in nodes:
        if j == origin or i == j:
            continue
        model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1, f"MTZ_{i}_{j}"

# (d) Fix the position of the origin in the MTZ ordering
#     (not a variable, but ensures consistency)
# No explicit constraint needed because origin is excluded from u.

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if model.status == pulp.LpStatusOptimal:
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes\n")

    # Build the tour starting from the origin
    tour = [origin]
    current = origin
    while True:
        # find the node j such that x[current,j] == 1
        next_node = None
        for j in nodes:
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:
                next_node = j
                break
        if next_node is None or next_node == origin:
            break
        tour.append(next_node)
        current = next_node
        if len(tour) == n:   # all nodes visited
            break
    tour.append(origin)  # close the circuit

    print("Optimal tour:")
    print(" -> ".join(tour))
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

travel_time = {
    ("Alpha", "Beta"):    209.8,
    ("Alpha", "Gamma"):   109.1,
    ("Alpha", "Delta"):    23.4,
    ("Alpha", "Epsilon"): 107.3,

    ("Beta", "Delta"):    214.1,
    ("Beta", "Epsilon"):  118.8,
    ("Beta", "Zeta"):     216.8,
    ("Gamma", "Delta"):    89.3,
    ("Gamma", "Epsilon"): 155.6,
    ("Gamma", "Zeta"):     24.7,
    ("Delta", "Epsilon"): 120.9,
    ("Delta", "Zeta"):     75.1,
    ("Epsilon", "Zeta"):  161.3,
}
# make the matrix symmetric
for i, j in list(travel_time.keys()):
    travel_time[(j, i)] = travel_time[(i, j)]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Binary decision variables: x[i,j] == 1 if we travel directly from i to j
x = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j:
            var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
            x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# Continuous order variables for MTZ subtour elimination
u = {}
for i in nodes:
    var_name = f"u_{i}"
    # u[origin] will be fixed later; others are bounded 1..n-1
    u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, upBound=n - 1, cat="Continuous")

origin = "Alpha"
# Fix the order of the origin node
model += u[origin] == 0, "Origin_Order_Fixed"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total travel time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(travel_time[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j), "Total_Time"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Exactly one outgoing edge from each node
for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{i}"

# 2) Exactly one incoming edge to each node
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1, f"In_{j}"

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination constraints (only for non‑origin nodes)
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j and i != origin and j != origin:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1, f"MTZ_{i}_{j}"

# 4) Order variable bounds for non‑origin nodes (already set by lowBound/upBound)
for i in nodes:
    if i != origin:
        model += u[i] >= 1, f"Order_LB_{i}"
        model += u[i] <= n - 1, f"Order_UB_{i}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal" or status == "Feasible":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes")

    # Reconstruct the tour
    tour = [origin]
    next_node = None
    while True:
        current = tour[-1]
        # find the successor of current
        for j in nodes:
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:
                next_node = j
                break
        if next_node is None or next_node == origin:
            break
        tour.append(next_node)

    tour.append(origin)  # close the circuit
    print("Tour order:")
    print(" -> ".join(tour))
else:
    print("No feasible solution found.")

"""
Traveling Salesman Problem for a dedicated cargo aircraft visiting 12 hubs.
The model uses binary edge variables and the Miller‑Tucker‑Zemlin (MTZ)
formulation for subtour elimination.
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
N = 12                                   # number of hubs
nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

# flight times (minutes) – symmetric matrix, values taken directly from the statement
dist = {
    (1, 2): 163.7, (1, 3): 198.5, (1, 4): 101.4, (1, 5): 68.3,  (1, 6): 116.7,
    (1, 7): 109.2, (1, 8): 109.2, (1, 9): 11.3,  (1,10): 96.8,  (1,11): 92.6,

    (4, 5): 50.8,  (4, 6): 75.2,  (4, 7): 162.4, (4, 8): 17.0,  (4, 9): 94.5,
    (4,10): 36.9,  (4,11): 17.0,  (4,12): 60.8,

    (5, 6): 52.4,  (5, 7): 111.8, (5, 8): 66.1,  (5, 9): 66.6,  (5,10): 72.1,
    (5,11): 34.9,  (5,12): 56.1,

    (6, 7): 115.3, (6, 8): 91.8,  (6, 9): 117.2, (6,10): 109.5, (6,11): 60.4,
    (6,12): 107.2,

    (7, 8): 177.9, (7, 9): 119.2, (7,10): 180.4, (7,11): 145.9, (7,12): 146.0,

    (8, 9): 101.0, (8,10): 26.4,  (8,11): 33.8,  (8,12): 63.3,

    (9,10): 87.1,  (9,11): 87.3,  (9,12): 40.5,

    (10,11): 49.1, (10,12): 46.7,

    (11,12): 59.4,
}

# make the matrix symmetric
for (i, j), d in list(dist.items()):
    dist[(j, i)] = d

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("CargoAircraft_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i,j] = 1 if the aircraft flies directly from i to j, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# MTZ auxiliary variables (continuous) to eliminate subtours
# u[1] is fixed to 0, others are in [1, N-1]
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "u",
    (i for i in nodes),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=N - 1,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total flight time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(dist[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Exactly one outgoing edge from each hub
for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1

# 2) Exactly one incoming edge to each hub
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination
# Fix u[1] = 0
model += u[1] == 0

for i in nodes:
    if i == 1:
        continue
    # bounds for MTZ variables (already defined by lowBound/upBound)
    model += u[i] >= 1
    model += u[i] <= N - 1

for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i == j or i == 1 or j == 1:
            continue
        model += u[i] - u[j] + N * x[(i, j)] <= N - 1

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    # total distance
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total flight time: {total_time:.2f} minutes")

    # reconstruct the tour
    tour = []
    current = 1
    visited = set()
    while True:
        visited.add(current)
        tour.append(current)
        # find the successor
        nxt = None
        for j in nodes:
            if j != current and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:
                nxt = j
                break
        if nxt is None or nxt in visited:
            break
        current = nxt
        if current == 1:
            break
    tour.append(1)  # return to origin
    print("Optimal tour (hub sequence):")
    print(" -> ".join(map(str, tour)))
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

# symmetric distance matrix (minutes)
dist = {}
def add(i, j, d):
    dist[(i, j)] = d
    dist[(j, i)] = d

add(0, 1, 142.7)   # Alpha - Beta
add(0, 2, 51.7)    # Alpha - Gamma
add(0, 3, 109.5)   # Alpha - Delta
add(0, 4, 91.4)    # Alpha - Epsilon
add(0, 5, 91.3)    # Alpha - Zeta
add(0, 6, 163.4)   # Alpha - Eta
add(0, 7, 37.8)    # Alpha - Theta
add(0, 8, 51.4)    # Alpha - Iota
add(0, 9, 72.1)    # Alpha - Kappa

add(1, 2, 95.9)    # Beta - Gamma
add(1, 3, 101.8)   # Beta - Delta
add(1, 4, 135.4)   # Beta - Epsilon
add(1, 5, 106.8)   # Beta - Zeta
add(1, 6, 23.6)    # Beta - Eta

add(1, 8, 91.4)    # Beta - Iota
add(1, 9, 83.2)    # Beta - Kappa

add(2, 3, 99.8)    # Gamma - Delta

add(2, 6, 118.3)   # Gamma - Eta
add(2, 7, 84.7)    # Gamma - Theta
add(2, 8, 19.0)    # Gamma - Iota
add(2, 9, 21.1)    # Gamma - Kappa

add(3, 4, 41.0)    # Delta - Epsilon
add(3, 5, 147.0)   # Delta - Zeta
add(3, 6, 108.2)   # Delta - Eta
add(3, 7, 107.2)   # Delta - Theta
add(3, 8, 81.0)    # Delta - Iota
add(3, 9, 109.0)   # Delta - Kappa

add(4, 5, 154.0)   # Epsilon - Zeta
add(4, 6, 145.5)   # Epsilon - Eta
add(4, 7, 76.5)    # Epsilon - Theta
add(4, 8, 84.2)    # Epsilon - Iota
add(4, 9, 118.0)   # Epsilon - Kappa

add(5, 6, 130.1)   # Zeta - Eta

add(8, 9, 34.5)    # Iota - Kappa

# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

x = {}

    for j in range(n):
        if i != j:
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"x_{i}_{j}", cat="Binary")
            x[(i, j)] = var

# MTZ order variables u[i] (continuous)
u = {}
for i in range(n):
    if i == 0:
        # fix the depot (Alpha) to order 1
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=1, upBound=1, cat="Continuous")
    else:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(f"u_{i}", lowBound=2, upBound=n, cat="Continuous")

# Objective: minimise total travel time
model += pulp.lpSum(dist[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in x), "TotalTravelTime"

# Each node has exactly one outgoing arc
for i in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"Out_{i}"

# Each node has exactly one incoming arc
for j in range(n):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in range(n) if i != j) == 1, f"In_{j}"

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
# For all i != j, i!=0, j!=0
for i in range(1, n):
    for j in range(1, n):
        if i != j:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1, f"MTZ_{i}_{j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes")

    # Reconstruct the tour
    tour = [0]          # start at Alpha (index 0)
    while len(tour) < n:
        last = tour[-1]
        for j in range(n):
            if last != j and pulp.value(x[(last, j)]) > 0.5:
                tour.append(j)
                break
    tour.append(0)  # return to start

    named_tour = " -> ".join(node_names[i] for i in tour)
    print("Optimal tour:")
    print(named_tour)
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

    pair(7, 8): 77.8,
    pair(7, 9): 105.8,
    pair(8, 9): 34.5,
}

n = len(facilities)

# Build a full distance matrix (symmetric, zero diagonal)
dist = [[0.0 for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
for (i, j), d in raw_times.items():
    dist[i][j] = d
    dist[j][i] = d  # symmetry

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Technician_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: x[i][j] = 1 if the tour goes directly from i to j

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Traveling Salesman Problem for 8 branch offices (quarterly reviews)
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# The manager must visit every office exactly once and return to the start.
# Travel times (in minutes) between offices are given partially.
# Missing travel times are set to a very large value (1e6) so that the
# optimizer will avoid them unless absolutely necessary.
# --------------------------------------------------------------

import pulp

# -------------------------
# 1. Data
# -------------------------
n = 8  # number of offices, indexed 1..8

# Given travel times (symmetric).  Each tuple is (i, j, time).
given_times = [
    (1, 2, 122.2),
    (1, 3, 137.2),
    (1, 4, 114.5),
    (1, 5, 149.5),
    (1, 6, 190.5),
    (1, 7, 114.4),
    (1, 8, 120.0),
    (2, 3, 121.3),
    (2, 4, 51.0),
    (2, 5, 111.4),
    (2, 6, 173.1),
    (2, 7, 31.0),
    (2, 8, 7.2),
    # (The remaining pairwise times are not supplied in the statement.
    #  They are filled with a very large placeholder value.)
]

# Build a complete distance dictionary d[(i,j)] for i != j
MISSING = 1e6  # penalty for missing data
d = {}
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        if i == j:
            continue
        d[(i, j)] = MISSING

# Fill in the symmetric values that we know
for i, j, t in given_times:
    d[(i, j)] = t
    d[(j, i)] = t  # symmetry

# -------------------------
# 2. Model
# -------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Quarterly_Review_Tour", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: x[i,j] = 1 if we travel directly from i to j
x = {}
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        if i != j:
            var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
            x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# MTZ ordering variables u[i] (continuous, bounds 1..n)
u = {}
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    var_name = f"u_{i}"
    # u[1] will be fixed to 1 later
    u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=1, upBound=n, cat="Continuous")

# -------------------------
# 3. Objective: minimise total travel time
# -------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(d[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in range(1, n + 1)
                                          for j in range(1, n + 1) if i != j)

# -------------------------
# 4. Constraints
# -------------------------

# 4.1 Each office is departed from exactly once
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in range(1, n + 1) if i != j) == 1, f"Depart_{i}"

# 4.2 Each office is arrived at exactly once
for j in range(1, n + 1):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in range(1, n + 1) if i != j) == 1, f"Arrive_{j}"

# Fix the order of the first node (office 1) to 1
model += u[1] == 1, "Fix_u1"

for i in range(2, n + 1):
    model += u[i] >= 2, f"u_lower_{i}"
    model += u[i] <= n, f"u_upper_{i}"

    for j in range(2, n + 1):

        # u_i - u_j + n * x_ij <= n-1
        model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1, f"MTZ_{i}_{j}"

# -------------------------
# 5. Solve
# -------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# -------------------------
# 6. Output
# -------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimum total travel time: {total_time:.2f} minutes")
    # Reconstruct the tour

    current = 1  # start at office 1 (arbitrary)

    while True:
        visited.add(current)
        tour.append(current)
        # find the next node

        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:

        if next_node is None or next_node in visited:
            break

}

            x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# MTZ auxiliary variables (continuous)
u = {}
for i in nodes:
    var_name = f"u_{i}"
    # u[1] will be fixed later; others bounded between 2 and n
    if i == 1:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=1, upBound=1, cat="Continuous")
    else:
        u[i] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=2, upBound=n, cat="Continuous")

# Objective: minimize total travel time
model += pulp.lpSum(dist[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)

# Constraints
# 1) Exactly one outgoing arc from each node
for i in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in nodes if i != j) == 1

# 2) Exactly one incoming arc to each node
for j in nodes:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1

# 3) MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j and i != 1 and j != 1:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[(i, j)] <= n - 1

# ---------- Solve ----------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ---------- Output ----------
if pulp.LpStatus[model.status] != "Optimal":
    print("No optimal solution found.")
else:
    # Build the tour
    tour = []
    current = 1
    visited = set()
    while True:
        visited.add(current)
        for j in nodes:
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[(current, j)]) > 0.5:
                tour.append((current, j))
                current = j
                break
        if current == 1:
            break

    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print("Optimal tour (order of visits):")
    order = [1]

The model uses binary arc variables and MTZ subtour elimination.
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.

import pulp

# ---------- data ----------
offices = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

# travel times (minutes) – symmetric matrix
travel = {
    (1, 2): 88.0,   (2, 1): 88.0,
    (1, 3): 124.3,  (3, 1): 124.3,
    (1, 4): 104.8,  (4, 1): 104.8,
    (1, 5): 78.2,   (5, 1): 78.2,
    (1, 6): 123.3,  (6, 1): 123.3,
    (2, 3): 101.3,  (3, 2): 101.3,
    (2, 4): 32.6,   (4, 2): 32.6,
    (2, 5): 106.2,  (5, 2): 106.2,
    (2, 6): 81.4,   (6, 2): 81.4,
    (3, 4): 75.2,   (4, 3): 75.2,
    (3, 5): 186.6,  (5, 3): 186.6,
    (3, 6): 27.1,   (6, 3): 27.1,
    (4, 5): 137.1,  (5, 4): 137.1,
    (4, 6): 51.7,   (6, 4): 51.7,
    (5, 6): 176.3,  (6, 5): 176.3,
}

# ---------- model ----------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Branch_Visit_TSP", pulp.LpMinimize)

# binary decision variables: x[i][j] = 1 if we travel directly from i to j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x",
                          ((i, j) for i in offices for j in offices if i != j),
                          lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# MTZ ordering variables (continuous but bounded to integer values 2..n)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("u", offices, lowBound=0, upBound=len(offices), cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Objective: minimise total travel time
model += pulp.lpSum(travel[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in offices for j in offices if i != j)

# ---------- constraints ----------
# each office has exactly one outgoing arc
for i in offices:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in offices if i != j) == 1

# each office has exactly one incoming arc
for j in offices:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in offices if i != j) == 1

# MTZ subtour elimination (fix u[1] = 1)
model += u[1] == 1
for i in offices:
    if i != 1:
        model += u[i] >= 2
        model += u[i] <= len(offices)

# MTZ constraints for all i != j, i != 1, j != 1
n = len(offices)
for i in offices:
    for j in offices:
        if i != j and i != 1 and j != 1:
            model += u[i] - u[j] + n * x[i, j] <= n - 1

# ---------- solve ----------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ---------- output ----------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    total_time = pulp.value(model.objective)
    print(f"Minimal total travel time: {total_time:.1f} minutes")

    # reconstruct tour
    tour = []
    current = 1  # start at office 1 (arbitrary, any node works)
    visited = set()
    while True:
        visited.add(current)
        tour.append(current)
        # find the successor
        next_office = None
        for j in offices:
            if current != j and pulp.value(x[current, j]) > 0.5:
                next_office = j
                break
        if next_office is None or next_office in visited:
            break
        current = next_office
        if len(visited) == len(offices):
            # close the tour back to the start
            tour.append(1)
            break

    print("Optimal visit order (including return to start):")
    print(" -> ".join(str(o) for o in tour))
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Transportation model – allocate workload from source clusters (S) to destination
data‑centers (D) so that total latency is minimal.

Supplies (capacity) and demands (required workload) are taken directly from the
statement.  Decision variables are continuous (non‑negative) because the
problem does not require integer‑only assignments; the linear program will
automatically produce integer values when the data are integral.

The model is solved with PuLP using the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
sources = ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S6", "S7"]
demands = ["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4", "D5", "D6", "D7"]

# supply of each source cluster
supply = {
    "S1": 136,
    "S2": 83,
    "S3": 146,
    "S4": 89,
    "S5": 91,
    "S6": 96,
    "S7": 92,
}

# demand of each destination data centre
demand = {
    "D1": 7,
    "D2": 54,
    "D3": 106,
    "D4": 143,
    "D5": 89,
    "D6": 110,
    "D7": 115,
}

# latency per unit (cost) matrix, rows = sources, columns = destinations
latency = {
    ("S1", "D1"): 8,  ("S1", "D2"): 18, ("S1", "D3"): 8,  ("S1", "D4"): 10,
    ("S1", "D5"): 16, ("S1", "D6"): 7,  ("S1", "D7"): 12,

    ("S2", "D1"): 19, ("S2", "D2"): 15, ("S2", "D3"): 15, ("S2", "D4"): 10,
    ("S2", "D5"): 13, ("S2", "D6"): 17, ("S2", "D7"): 17,

    ("S3", "D1"): 14, ("S3", "D2"): 6,  ("S3", "D3"): 7,  ("S3", "D4"): 20,
    ("S3", "D5"): 5,  ("S3", "D6"): 9,  ("S3", "D7"): 2,

    ("S4", "D1"): 16, ("S4", "D2"): 12, ("S4", "D3"): 18, ("S4", "D4"): 4,
    ("S4", "D5"): 17, ("S4", "D6"): 4,  ("S4", "D7"): 10,

    ("S5", "D1"): 3,  ("S5", "D2"): 6,  ("S5", "D3"): 9,  ("S5", "D4"): 15,
    ("S5", "D5"): 17, ("S5", "D6"): 5,  ("S5", "D7"): 14,

    ("S6", "D1"): 3,  ("S6", "D2"): 8,  ("S6", "D3"): 15, ("S6", "D4"): 12,
    ("S6", "D5"): 1,  ("S6", "D6"): 14, ("S6", "D7"): 2,

    ("S7", "D1"): 13, ("S7", "D2"): 17, ("S7", "D3"): 12, ("S7", "D4"): 8,
    ("S7", "D5"): 13, ("S7", "D6"): 3,  ("S7", "D7"): 12,
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Workload_Distribution_MinLatency", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: amount shipped from source i to destination j
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in sources for j in demands),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Objective: minimise total latency
model += pulp.lpSum(latency[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in sources for j in demands), "Total_Latency"

# Supply constraints (capacity of each source, may be partially unused)
for i in sources:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for j in demands) <= supply[i],
        f"Supply_{i}",
    )

# Demand constraints (must satisfy each destination exactly)
for j in demands:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[i, j] for i in sources) == demand[j],
        f"Demand_{j}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    ("R2", "H5"): 11, ("R2", "H6"): 3,  ("R2", "H7"): 19,

    ("R3", "H5"): 5,  ("R3", "H6"): 20, ("R3", "H7"): 3,

    ("R4", "H1"): 10, ("R4", "H2"): 18, ("R4", "H3"): 13, ("R4", "H4"): 11,
    ("R4", "H5"): 5,  ("R4", "H6"): 17, ("R4", "H7"): 3,

    ("R5", "H1"): 14, ("R5", "H2"): 17, ("R5", "H3"): 12, ("R5", "H4"): 1,
    ("R5", "H5"): 12, ("R5", "H6"): 10, ("R5", "H7"): 6,

    ("R6", "H1"): 7,  ("R6", "H2"): 11, ("R6", "H3"): 16, ("R6", "H4"): 7,
    ("R6", "H5"): 8,  ("R6", "H6"): 5,  ("R6", "H7"): 5,

    ("R7", "H1"): 3,  ("R7", "H2"): 10, ("R7", "H3"): 4,  ("R7", "H4"): 17,
    ("R7", "H5"): 18, ("R7", "H6"): 17, ("R7", "H7"): 2,
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Medical_Supplies_Distribution", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: amount shipped from warehouse r to health center h
x = {}
for r in supply:
    for h in demand:
        var_name = f"x_{r}_{h}"
        x[(r, h)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Objective: minimize total transportation cost
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(r, h)] * x[(r, h)] for (r, h) in x), "Total_Cost"

# Supply constraints (cannot ship more than inventory at each warehouse)
for r, cap in supply.items():
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(r, h)] for h in demand) <= cap, f"Supply_{r}"

for h, req in demand.items():
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(r, h)] for r in supply) >= req, f"Demand_{h}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    print(f"  {r}: used {used:.2f} / available {supply[r]}")

for h in demand:
    received = sum(x[(r, h)].varValue for r in supply if x[(r, h)].varValue is not None)
    print(f"  {h}: received {received:.2f} / required {demand[h]}")
