# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Optimal fuel allocation from vessels to ports minimizing total fuel consumption.

Data:
    Vessels (capacity in kiloliters):
        Alpha   194
        Beta     56
        Gamma    71
        Delta   159
        Epsilon  84

    Ports (demand in kiloliters):
        P1  60
        P2  85
        P3 106
        P4 148
        P5 110

    Consumption rate (fuel consumption per kiloliter shipped):
                P1  P2  P3  P4  P5
        Alpha   13   9  14   9   3
        Beta    16   1  18   2  12
        Gamma    8   3   2   1   8
        Delta    7   1  20   5   8
        Epsilon  5  16   4  19   7
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Sets
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
vessels = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon"]
ports   = ["P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5"]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Parameters
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
capacity = {
    "Alpha":   194,
    "Beta":     56,
    "Gamma":    71,
    "Delta":   159,
    "Epsilon": 84,
}

demand = {
    "P1": 60,
    "P2": 85,
    "P3": 106,
    "P4": 148,
    "P5": 110,
}

# consumption_rate[v][p] = fuel consumption (units) per kiloliter shipped
consumption_rate = {
    "Alpha":   {"P1": 13, "P2": 9,  "P3": 14, "P4": 9,  "P5": 3},
    "Beta":    {"P1": 16, "P2": 1,  "P3": 18, "P4": 2,  "P5": 12},
    "Gamma":   {"P1": 8,  "P2": 3,  "P3": 2,  "P4": 1,  "P5": 8},
    "Delta":   {"P1": 7,  "P2": 1,  "P3": 20, "P4": 5,  "P5": 8},
    "Epsilon": {"P1": 5,  "P2": 16, "P3": 4,  "P4": 19, "P5": 7},
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Decision variables
#    x[v][p] = amount (kiloliters) shipped from vessel v to port p
#    Continuous, ≥ 0
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((v, p) for v in vessels for p in ports),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Fuel_Allocation_Min_Consumption", pulp.LpMinimize)

# 4.1 Objective: minimise total fuel consumption
model += pulp.lpSum(
    consumption_rate[v][p] * x[(v, p)] for v in vessels for p in ports
), "Total_Consumption"

# 4.2 Vessel capacity constraints
for v in vessels:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(v, p)] for p in ports) <= capacity[v],
        f"Cap_{v}",
    )

# 4.3 Port demand constraints (must be satisfied exactly)
for p in ports:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(v, p)] for v in vessels) == demand[p],
        f"Demand_{p}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print(f"Objective (total consumption): {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Shipment plan (kiloliters from vessel → port):")
for v in vessels:
    for p in ports:
        qty = x[(v, p)].value()
        if qty is not None and qty > 1e-6:  # display only positive shipments
            print(f"  {v} → {p}: {qty:.2f}")

print("\nVessel utilizations:")
for v in vessels:
    used = sum(x[(v, p)].value() for p in ports)
    print(f"  {v}: {used:.2f} / {capacity[v]}  ({used / capacity[v] * 100:.1f}%)")

# to minimize total latency cost.

import pulp

# ------------------------------
# Data
# ------------------------------

# Sources (clusters) with their processing capacities
sources = {
    "X1": 64,
    "X2": 108,
    "X3": 58,
}

# Destinations (data centers) with required computational loads
destinations = {
    "Y1": 59,
    "Y2": 10,
    "Y3": 133,
}

# Unit latency cost matrix (source -> destination)
cost = {
    ("X1", "Y1"): 19, ("X1", "Y2"): 11, ("X1", "Y3"): 7,
    ("X2", "Y1"): 16, ("X2", "Y2"): 13, ("X2", "Y3"): 15,
    ("X3", "Y1"): 5,  ("X3", "Y2"): 9,  ("X3", "Y3"): 5,
}

# ------------------------------
# Model
# ------------------------------

# Create a minimization problem
model = pulp.LpProblem("Workload_Allocation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: amount shipped from source i to destination j (continuous, >=0)
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "ship",
    ((i, j) for i in sources for j in destinations),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Objective: minimize total latency cost
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in sources for j in destinations), "Total_Latency"

# Supply constraints: each source cannot exceed its capacity
for i, cap in sources.items():
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in destinations) <= cap,
        f"Supply_{i}",
    )

# Demand constraints: each destination must receive exactly its required load
for j, demand in destinations.items():
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in sources) == demand,
        f"Demand_{j}",
    )

# ------------------------------
# Solve
# ------------------------------

# Solve with HiGHS (no console messages, 2‑minute time limit)
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ------------------------------
# Output
# ------------------------------

# Print status
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])

# Print optimal objective value
print("Minimum total latency cost:", pulp.value(model.objective))

    for j in destinations:

    used = sum(x[(i, j)].varValue for j in destinations)
    print(f"  {i}: {used:.2f} / {sources[i]}")

print("\nDemand fulfillment:")
for j in destinations:
    received = sum(x[(i, j)].varValue for i in sources)
    print(f"  {j}: {received:.2f} / {destinations[j]}")

# solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver

import pulp

# ----- data ---------------------------------------------------------

# Sources (server clusters) and their capacities
sources = ["Alpha1", "Alpha2", "Alpha3", "Alpha4", "Alpha5", "Alpha6"]
supply = {
    "Alpha1": 110,
    "Alpha2": 123,
    "Alpha3": 108,
    "Alpha4": 73,
    "Alpha5": 161,
    "Alpha6": 75,
}

# Destinations (processing jobs) and their required loads
destinations = ["Beta1", "Beta2", "Beta3", "Beta4", "Beta5", "Beta6"]
demand = {
    "Beta1": 244,
    "Beta2": 35,
    "Beta3": 58,
    "Beta4": 103,
    "Beta5": 10,
    "Beta6": 112,
}

# Unit latency cost matrix (source → destination)
cost = {
    ("Alpha1", "Beta1"): 2,  ("Alpha1", "Beta2"): 10, ("Alpha1", "Beta3"): 12,
    ("Alpha1", "Beta4"): 12, ("Alpha1", "Beta5"): 14, ("Alpha1", "Beta6"): 5,

    ("Alpha2", "Beta1"): 8,  ("Alpha2", "Beta2"): 17, ("Alpha2", "Beta3"): 14,
    ("Alpha2", "Beta4"): 19, ("Alpha2", "Beta5"): 6,  ("Alpha2", "Beta6"): 6,

    ("Alpha3", "Beta1"): 6,  ("Alpha3", "Beta2"): 3,  ("Alpha3", "Beta3"): 20,
    ("Alpha3", "Beta4"): 13, ("Alpha3", "Beta5"): 20, ("Alpha3", "Beta6"): 8,

    ("Alpha4", "Beta1"): 16, ("Alpha4", "Beta2"): 19, ("Alpha4", "Beta3"): 5,
    ("Alpha4", "Beta4"): 8,  ("Alpha4", "Beta5"): 15, ("Alpha4", "Beta6"): 9,

    ("Alpha5", "Beta1"): 15, ("Alpha5", "Beta2"): 9,  ("Alpha5", "Beta3"): 1,
    ("Alpha5", "Beta4"): 15, ("Alpha5", "Beta5"): 10, ("Alpha5", "Beta6"): 18,

    ("Alpha6", "Beta1"): 6,  ("Alpha6", "Beta2"): 3,  ("Alpha6", "Beta3"): 15,
    ("Alpha6", "Beta4"): 12, ("Alpha6", "Beta5"): 19, ("Alpha6", "Beta6"): 10,
}

# ----- model ---------------------------------------------------------

model = pulp.LpProblem("Latency_Minimization", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: amount shipped from each source to each destination
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x", (sources, destinations), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Objective: minimise total latency cost
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(i, j)] * x[i][j] for i in sources for j in destinations)

# Supply constraints (cannot exceed available capacity)
for i in sources:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i][j] for j in destinations) <= supply[i], f"Supply_{i}"

# Demand constraints (must satisfy exact job load)
for j in destinations:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i][j] for i in sources) == demand[j], f"Demand_{j}"

# ----- solve ----------------------------------------------------------

model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----- output ---------------------------------------------------------

print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print(f"Total latency cost = {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Optimal allocation (units shipped from Alpha → Beta):")

}

betas   = list(demand.keys())

"""
Optimal allocation of cargo aircraft to regional hubs
minimising total fuel consumption (cost per ton).

The model is a classic transportation problem:
    - Decision variables x[(i,j)] = tons shipped from aircraft i to hub j
    - Objective: minimise Σ  cost[i][j] * x[(i,j)]
    - Supply constraints: Σ_j x[(i,j)] ≤ capacity_i  for every aircraft i
    - Demand constraints: Σ_i x[(i,j)] = demand_j   for every hub j
All data are entered explicitly; no external files are read.
"""

import pulp

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Aircraft (Alpha) identifiers and their cargo capacities (tons)
aircraft = ["Alpha-1", "Alpha-2", "Alpha-3", "Alpha-4", "Alpha-5",
            "Alpha-6", "Alpha-7", "Alpha-8", "Alpha-9"]
capacity = {
    "Alpha-1": 155,
    "Alpha-2": 163,
    "Alpha-3": 105,
    "Alpha-4": 72,
    "Alpha-5": 75,
    "Alpha-6": 85,
    "Alpha-7": 81,
    "Alpha-8": 200,
    "Alpha-9": 148,
}

# Hubs (Beta) identifiers and required deliveries (tons)
hubs = ["Beta-1", "Beta-2", "Beta-3", "Beta-4", "Beta-5",
        "Beta-6", "Beta-7", "Beta-8", "Beta-9"]
demand = {
    "Beta-1": 69,
    "Beta-2": 127,
    "Beta-3": 40,
    "Beta-4": 103,
    "Beta-5": 39,
    "Beta-6": 95,
    "Beta-7": 115,
    "Beta-8": 45,
    "Beta-9": 150,
}

# Fuel consumption rate (cost per ton) for each aircraft‑hub pair
# Rows correspond to aircraft in the order given above,
# columns correspond to hubs in the order given above.
cost_table = [
    # Beta-1 Beta-2 Beta-3 Beta-4 Beta-5 Beta-6 Beta-7 Beta-8 Beta-9
    [ 1,    10,    7,    17,    20,    17,    7,    13,    10],  # Alpha-1
    [ 2,     8,   16,    13,     4,    8,   16,    20,     3],  # Alpha-2
    [17,     1,   12,    11,     5,   13,   19,    14,    12],  # Alpha-3
    [18,     6,   16,     3,     1,   19,    3,     1,     9],  # Alpha-4
    [ 7,     2,    2,    13,    17,   10,   17,    14,    14],  # Alpha-5
    [13,     3,   18,    18,    20,    5,    9,     3,    10],  # Alpha-6
    [ 3,    17,    7,     5,    18,   11,   13,    19,     3],  # Alpha-7
    [10,    14,    8,     2,     8,    3,   14,     4,    15],  # Alpha-8
    [20,    20,    2,    10,     6,    4,    1,     5,     1],  # Alpha-9
]

        cost[(a, h)] = cost_table[i][j]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

model = pulp.LpProblem("Cargo_Allocation_Min_Fuel", pulp.LpMinimize)

                          lowBound=0,

# Transportation problem – minimum cost allocation
# ------------------------------------------------
# Plants (suppliers) with processing capacities
# Depots (customers) with required inventory levels
# Unit transportation costs from each plant to each depot
# Solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver

import pulp

# -------------------------
# Data
# -------------------------
plants = ["P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5", "P6", "P7", "P8"]
depots = ["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4", "D5", "D6", "D7", "D8"]

supply = {
    "P1": 64,
    "P2": 166,
    "P3": 83,
    "P4": 181,
    "P5": 156,
    "P6": 166,
    "P7": 194,
    "P8": 64,
}

demand = {
    "D1": 291,
    "D2": 134,
    "D3": 10,
    "D4": 110,
    "D5": 1,
    "D6": 94,
    "D7": 31,
    "D8": 183,
}

# Cost matrix (cost per unit shipped from plant i to depot j)
cost = {
    ("P1", "D1"): 3,  ("P1", "D2"): 18, ("P1", "D3"): 2,  ("P1", "D4"): 3,
    ("P1", "D5"): 16, ("P1", "D6"): 2,  ("P1", "D7"): 10, ("P1", "D8"): 14,

    ("P2", "D1"): 6,  ("P2", "D2"): 5,  ("P2", "D3"): 14, ("P2", "D4"): 12,
    ("P2", "D5"): 13, ("P2", "D6"): 15, ("P2", "D7"): 13, ("P2", "D8"): 13,

    ("P3", "D1"): 3,  ("P3", "D2"): 18, ("P3", "D3"): 5,  ("P3", "D4"): 12,
    ("P3", "D5"): 4,  ("P3", "D6"): 6,  ("P3", "D7"): 18, ("P3", "D8"): 13,

    ("P4", "D1"): 17, ("P4", "D2"): 5,  ("P4", "D3"): 8,  ("P4", "D4"): 1,
    ("P4", "D5"): 1,  ("P4", "D6"): 10, ("P4", "D7"): 15, ("P4", "D8"): 18,

    ("P5", "D1"): 14, ("P5", "D2"): 18, ("P5", "D3"): 13, ("P5", "D4"): 8,
    ("P5", "D5"): 8,  ("P5", "D6"): 15, ("P5", "D7"): 12, ("P5", "D8"): 5,

    ("P6", "D1"): 9,  ("P6", "D2"): 7,  ("P6", "D3"): 4,  ("P6", "D4"): 2,
    ("P6", "D5"): 14, ("P6", "D6"): 20, ("P6", "D7"): 1,  ("P6", "D8"): 8,

    ("P7", "D1"): 7,  ("P7", "D2"): 3,  ("P7", "D3"): 4,  ("P7", "D4"): 20,
    ("P7", "D5"): 2,  ("P7", "D6"): 15, ("P7", "D7"): 20, ("P7", "D8"): 2,

    ("P8", "D1"): 8,  ("P8", "D2"): 2,  ("P8", "D3"): 13, ("P8", "D4"): 15,
    ("P8", "D5"): 8,  ("P8", "D6"): 18, ("P8", "D7"): 7,  ("P8", "D8"): 2,
}

# -------------------------
# Model
# -------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("MinCost_Allocation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: amount shipped from plant i to depot j (integer, >=0)
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "ship",
    ((i, j) for i in plants for j in depots),
    lowBound=0,
    cat="Integer",
)

# Objective: minimise total transportation cost
model += pulp.lpSum(cost[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in plants for j in depots), "Total_Cost"

# Supply constraints (plant capacity)
for i in plants:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for j in depots) <= supply[i],
        f"Supply_{i}",

# Demand constraints (must meet exactly the required inventory)
for j in depots:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, j)] for i in plants) == demand[j],
        f"Demand_{j}",
    )

# -------------------------
# Solve
# -------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# -------------------------
# Output
# -------------------------
